Together, our results demonstrate that long-term N fertilization drives a conservative, microbially regulated P cycling strategy in which enhanced mineralization is tightly coupled with rapid immobilization, whereas P fertilization primarily increases soil P stocks. These findings highlight distinct microbial mechanisms regulating P cycling under contrasting nutrient inputs and underscore the importance of balanced fertilization for sustaining P availability while minimizing environmental losses.

title: Strengthening Key Technologies versus Process Reformations: A Comparison of the Low-Carbon Transition Pathways of China’s Iron and Steel Industry
abstract: Abstract As a hard-to-abate sector and an industrial backbone, the iron and steel industry involves a low-carbon transition that is crucial for China to achieve green growth and emission reduction targets. This study developed an innovative integrated iron&steel assessment model (IIAM), combining technology-choice modules with bottom-up technological analysis and top-down macroeconomic simulation to conduct low-carbon transition pathway analysis. In comparison with a carbon-reduction scenario in which reducing CO2 emissions relies on scaling down production and constrained economic growth, the planned national iron and steel industry development pathway has advantages in technological progress and structural adjustments. To realize potentially greater synergistic energy–environmental–economic benefits, two sets of substitutive low-carbon transition pathways are proposed on the basis of forward-looking technologies and production processes reformation. Among key technology deployment pathways, increasing scrap utilization is the preferred option, and hydrogen metallurgy excels in cleaning the energy mix. Production process reformation pathways can further unlock the potential for carbon mitigation, air-pollution control, resource use, and economic growth, yet they involve cost increases. The short-term strategy should prioritize existing long-process retrofitting, whereas the long-term transition should focus on scrap utilization, hydrogen-based metallurgy, and more breakthrough technological innovations.

title: A Source-Based Accounting of Microplastic Release into Freshwater in Mainland China from 2000 to 2022: Priorities and Gaps
abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs), mostly stemming from terrestrial activities, can be easily transported once they enter freshwater. Limited national-level accounting has constrained accurate global estimates, investigations of environmental fate, and the development of targeted management measures for MP pollution. In this context, this study estimated MP generation and its release into freshwater in China from 2000 to 2022, with a focus on 21 typical inland activities and products. An accumulation of 6.36 × 1021 MPs (36.39 million tonnes, Mt) was generated, of which 2.39 × 1021 items (20.12 Mt) were released into freshwater, equivalent to 1.82 trillion and 1.01 trillion 20-g plastic bottles, respectively. Urban and rural areas made distinct contributions to MP generation, with urban areas contributing a greater quantity (59.12%) and rural areas contributing a greater mass (79.60%). The most critical contributors to MP generation and freshwater release were identified as transportation-related sources by number (>99.9%) and agricultural sources by mass (>59.9%). This study provides a methodological basis for MP accounting, especially in areas lacking monitoring capabilities, and helps identify effective and efficient MP control strategies.

title: A High-Permeance Nanofiltration Membrane via Complementary Interface Engineering for Enhanced Selectivity between Mineral Salts and Emerging Pollutants
abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration (NF) membranes with high water permeance, superior emerging pollutant (EP) retention, and selective mineral salt passage are highly desirable for high-quality drinking water treatment, yet challenging due to the selectivity−permeance trade-off. Herein, a polyamide-based NF membrane was engineered via a complementary interface strategy involving (2-hydroxypropyl)-β-cyclodextrin (CD) doping and secondary sulfonamidation with sulfuryl chloride (SC). The resulting CD-PA-SC membrane exhibited excellent water permeance (26.9 L m−2 h−1 bar−1, 3.5- and 2.4-fold higher than NF 90 and NF 270), while maintaining high rejection for five typical EPs with diverse properties and selectively allowing the passage of dietary mineral ions. Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry analysis, transition state theory, MD simulation, and DFT calculations revealed that CD-PA-SC’s thinner and more hydrophilic active layer promotes water permeance; its more negative surface charge facilitates mineral ion passage; and the tailored pore size, together with the CD-enhanced intrapore diffusion resistance, ensures enhanced broad-spectrum EP rejection. Thus, CD-PA-SC combines high efficiency, a low carbon footprint, and healthy water production, with promising applications in secondary water supply and point-of-use purifiers. This complementary dual-step modification strategy offers new insights into designing NF membranes for multiobjective separations in advanced drinking water treatment.

title: A Safe and Just Earth by Design
abstract: Abstract Movement to a safe and just Earth system space for novel entities depends on the control of their quantities and/or qualities. Concerns about the adverse effects of such entities emphasize the momentous challenge of managing production and release volumes, but comparatively little attention has been paid to the control of novel entity quality (i.e., hazards). While control over chemical quantities may reduce exposure, if the inherent hazard has not been reduced or eliminated, even small quantities of hazardous substances can result in significant harm to the Earth system, people, and other forms of life if controls fail (which occur probabilistically). Such intraspecies, intergenerational, and intragenerational harm is unjust. Safer chemical design, which eliminates or reduces inherent hazards at the design stage while maximizing functionality, affords control over novel chemical entities and their adverse impacts. A large body of literature demonstrates that we can already manipulate the fate and transport, absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and specific interactions of novel entities by adjusting their physicochemical properties. Safer chemical design, therefore, enables the elimination of significant harm to present and future generations as well as to other species and maximizes the functional performance of essential molecules and materials. The ability to act via safer chemical design is evident. Whether action is taken remains to be determined.

title: Optimizing Ash Content in Biomass Hydrothermal Liquefaction through Machine Learning and Sustainability Assessment
abstract: Abstract Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a highly promising thermochemical technology for converting wet biomass into bioliquid fuels. However, the effects of ash content in process performance and sustainability remain poorly understood. This study examined acid washing, alkali washing, and feedstock blending as methods for altering the ash content in a given biomass feedstock. Machine learning tools were employed in sustainability assessment for a 200 t/day plant, using life cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis. Feedstock blending best reduced ash content (ash from 34.4 to 6.40 wt %). Ash content had opposing effects on product yield and oil quality. Across ash contents of 3.60–34.4 wt %, the oil higher heating value consistently rose, whereas oil yield initially increased then declined. The char yield followed an opposite trend. Integrated environmental and economic assessment identified 6.40 wt % ash as the optimal HTL condition for sludge and Chlorella. Under a boundary excluding biomass cultivation and harvesting, this condition gave an energy return on investment of 3.21 and a global warming potential of −317 kg CO2 eq/t dry biomass. The minimum fuel selling price was 0.517 $/L. These results show that reducing biomass ash content is not always advantageous. Feedstock blending demonstrated substantial benefits for large-scale oil production from high-ash biomass.

title: Gestational Exposure to Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals and Small Vulnerable Newborns: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Abstract Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) have been implicated in adverse birth outcomes, yet epidemiological findings remain inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate associations between gestational EDC exposure and small vulnerable newborns (SVNs), including preterm birth (PTB), low birth weight (LBW), and small for gestational age (SGA). PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from inception to January 5, 2026. A total of 106 observational studies involving 98,133 births from 31 countries were included. Higher prenatal exposure to several per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), and perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA), was associated with an increased risk of PTB, while PFOS was also associated with LBW. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), PFNA, PFDA, and perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) were positively associated with SGA. Among other EDCs, higher exposure to ∑DEHP, mono-2-cyclohexyl phthalate (MCPP), mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MECPP), monoisobutyl phthalate (MiBP), and bisphenol A (BPA) was associated with increased PTB risk. Stratified analyses suggested stronger associations in Asian populations, pregnancies with female fetuses, and countries without or with partial folic acid fortification. These findings indicate that prenatal exposure to PFAS and phthalates may increase the risk of SVNs, particularly PTB, and that population characteristics may modify these associations.

title: Contrasting Fate of Thallium and Cadmium in the Soil-Rice System: Convergent Rhizosphere Bioavailability Responses Yet Divergent Translocation and Grain Partitioning
abstract: Abstract Combined contamination of soils with thallium (Tl) and cadmium (Cd) is widespread. Despite comparable accumulation of Tl and Cd by rice plants, the mechanisms underlying significantly lower Tl concentrations than Cd in grains remain unclear. Here, pot experiments, rhizotron observations and field sampling were combined to investigate the fate of Tl/Cd across the soil-rice system. Sequential extraction shows that flooding decreased Tl/Cd mobility in bulk soil, with Cd enriched in the oxidizable fraction and Tl in the residual fraction. In the rhizosphere, planar optode and laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) reveals that flooding induced iron-plaque formation, restricting rice Tl/Cd uptake compared with continuous drainage. Tissue- and microscale-level (LA-ICP-MS) analyses show that Tl transfer from node-to-leaf was 3.00–8.85 times that of Cd which exhibited greater upward translocation. In brown rice, 66.0–86.0% of Cd transported to grains was allocated to the endosperm. In contrast, Tl was preferentially enriched in the embryo, which represented only 1.78–2.66% of the biomass but contained 42.9–60.8% of Tl, potentially associated with high K demand and K-related transport pathways. Thus, contrasting shoot translocation and brown rice partitioning patterns of Tl/Cd explain differential grain concentrations, offering mechanistic insights for safe rice production.

title: Emissions from Gas Distribution and Postmeter Leaks May Drive Seasonal and Diurnal Trends in Methane Emissions in Baltimore
abstract: Abstract We estimated diurnal and seasonal trends in methane (CH4) emissions and evaluated their relationships with trends in natural gas usage data in Baltimore, MD, USA. We used Monin-Obukhov Similarity Theory for flux estimation at urban, suburban, and rural sites using several years of tower mole fraction measurements and compared flux estimates to hourly natural gas usage data for one year at the urban sites. A diurnal pattern with larger daytime emissions is present at all sites and lags a similar diurnal pattern in natural gas usage at sites where usage data is available, suggesting the diurnal trends are related to postmeter emissions. The estimates show a seasonal trend and higher emissions at the urban sites which we expect is related to natural gas distribution pipeline leaks and leak maintenance schedules. These seasonal trends are absent at the suburban sites which are in areas where pipelines have likely been upgraded. Our results reinforce that postmeter gas emissions are likely an important source of urban CH4 emissions. We expect that gas pipeline leak maintenance schedules play an important role driving seasonal CH4 emissions trends, and differences in pipe material can cause within-city variability in CH4 emissions magnitudes and trends.

title: Calcium-Dependent Rapid Adaptation to Long-Term Warming in Zooplankton
abstract: Abstract Climate change is rapidly warming freshwater habitats. Here, we employed the model freshwater zooplankton Daphnia magna to address whether long-term heat selection leads to increased tolerance, and whether this adaptive response is constrained by calcium availability and regulation. We showed that D. magna populations exhibited a robust adaptive response following multigenerational selection, with increased heat tolerance and shifted phenotypic plasticity. However, this tolerance was accompanied by temperature-dependent trade-offs in growth and reproductive timing that may accumulate over generations. Such enhanced heat tolerance was contingent upon sufficient environmental calcium, with performance declining under calcium-limited conditions, thereby uncovering a previously underexplored but ecologically significant phenomenon of the calcium dependency of heat tolerance. Novel real-time near-infrared (NIR-II-Ca) imaging demonstrated that heat adaptation involved not only increased calcium demand but also an adaptive optimization of calcium flux dynamics. This physiological shift is further supported by the constitutive up-regulation of heat shock transcription factor (HSF). By mapping the HSF-centered regulatory network, we revealed that HSF may coordinate a systemic program beyond canonical stress paradigms, integrating ion homeostasis with heat tolerance. Collectively, our study highlights that while rapid adaptation to warming is feasible, it is fundamentally constrained by internal trade-offs and external calcium dependency, underscoring the complex interplay of physiology, environment, and molecular regulation in determining organismal resilience to climate warming.

title: Significant Near-Term Inequity under China’s 2035 NDC due to a Time Lag in Mitigation Effects across Regions
abstract: Abstract China has submitted its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) toward 2035, potentially promoting its simultaneous goals of mitigating climate change and improving air quality. Yet, the effects of this NDC remain unclear across regions and over time. By using an integrated modeling framework, we show that the NDC increases the net benefits of these simultaneous goals by 1500.5 billion USD over 2025–2060, with significant heterogeneity across space and time. In the near term, the NDC reduces climate benefits, particularly in underdeveloped regions, primarily due to increased coal-based power generation needed to balance renewable intermittency and soil organic carbon release by rapid afforestation. In the long term, the NDC generates 3924.3 billion USD in climate benefits and 1659.5 billion USD in health cobenefits, benefiting all regions, although remaining concentrated in high-income regions. Extra measures are needed to enhance policy coherence under the NDC target, with earlier afforestation, non-CO2 abatement, and compensation mechanisms being central.

title: A New Strategy of Electron Injection for Contaminant Reduction in Groundwater
abstract: Abstract In situ chemical reduction (ISCR) is an efficient process for groundwater remediation, whereas the injection of reductants poses secondary contamination risks. Here, we propose a new strategy of electron injection for contaminant reduction in groundwater without the injection of reductants. The reductants are physically separated from the contaminants in aquifers, and electron transfer from reductants to contaminants was achieved by two connected electrodes due to the potential difference. Results showed that 0.1 mM Cr(VI) (pH 2.5) was removed by 98% within 2 h in a laboratory batch system using 10 mM sodium dithionite (pH 11.8) as the electron source. Electrochemically stable electrodes, such as graphite and mixed metal oxides, exhibited high performance in Cr(VI) removal. Over 85% of Cr(VI) removal was maintained in 10 cycles of consecutive treatments. This electron injection system could remove 81% of Cr(VI) within 60 h in a simulated aquifer. By leveraging electron injection, this approach provides a feasible pathway for aquifer redox regulation, thereby reducing the reliance on massive chemical inputs and minimizing secondary environmental disturbances caused by traditional ISCR.

title: Experimental p K a Values of Substituted and Unsubstituted Perfluoroalkyl Sulfonamides Via 19F NMR
abstract: Abstract Perfluoroalkyl sulfonamides (FASAs) are a class of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) found throughout the environment in water, soil, and biota. Sorption behavior, bioaccumulation, and environmental longevity of ionogenic molecules like FASAs is governed by the acid dissociation constant (pKa). However, limited experimental pKa values are available for FASAs, with most values computationally modeled with unknown accuracy. In this research 19F Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy was used to experimentally determine the pKa of perfluorobutane sulfonamide (FBSA) (6.22 ± 0.06), N-methyl (Me) FBSA (7.46 ± 0.03), perfluorohexane sulfonamide (FHxSA) (6.22 ± 0.04), perfluorooctane sulfonamide (FOSA) (6.4 ± 0.3), Me-FOSA (7.7 ± 0.3), and N-ethyl FOSA (8.0 ± 0.3). The pKa of low aqueous solubility FASAs (FOSA, MeFOSA, and EtFOSA) were determined using acetonitrile (ACN):aqueous buffer mixtures and an aggregated mathematical approach developed to simultaneously fit the data for 40, 50, and 60% ACN. Fluorinated carbon number did not significantly impact pKa. Methyl substitution of nitrogen (MeFBSA) increased the pKa by 1.24 log units for C4 and 1.3 log units for C8 FASAs. Ethyl substitution increased the pKa by 1.6 log units (FOSA vs EtFOSA). Experimentally measured values were compared to four different prediction models. Our internally corrected DFT model gave the best agreement with experimental values while Chemicalize gave pKa values up to 4 log units lower than experimental values.

title: Understanding Unexpected Ozone–Health Associations: Are Secondary Oxidative Pollutants Key?
abstract: Abstract Despite the well-established mechanisms of how ozone (O3) results in adverse health, it is not uncommon for population-based epidemiology studies to find evidence that lower O3 levels are associated with higher risks of disease. Common explanations, such as the scavenging of O3 by nitric oxide near traffic and differential measurement error, cannot fully explain these unexpected associations. Therefore, we propose an alternate explanation for counter-to-hypothesized associations for O3. Specifically, we hypothesize that observed associations between higher levels of O3 and better health outcomes could be a consequence of the complex atmospheric chemistry that occurs in urban and near-urban areas. Low O3 could coincide with active oxidative processes, either through O3 consumption or parallel pathways involving other oxidants. Since these processes can generate toxic but unmeasured secondary products, it would be unsurprising to find inverse associations with O3. In this perspective, we highlight the key evidence supporting this hypothesis. In doing so, we hope that this perspective may inform future plans for air quality measurement and provide context for the interpretation of associations between O3 and health in epidemiology studies.

title: Predicting Bioconcentration Factors and Concentrations of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Plants with Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Bioconcentration factors (BCF) and concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in crops were predicted by four machine learning models using a newly compiled data set composed of 11 crops, 11 plant tissue compartments, and 21 PFAS, as well as diverse soil properties and cultivation conditions. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) achieved the best performance, with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.951 for Log BCF and 0.943 for Log C. Feature importance analysis showed that soil pH and PFAS carbon chain length are key predictors of BCF. Soil PFAS concentration is the primary input feature for PFAS concentrations in plants and shorter growth-cycle plants accumulated higher PFAS concentrations. Root and leaf tissues were distinguished as the primary compartments of PFAS accumulation, exhibiting the highest BCF and concentration levels. Interestingly, although PFAS accumulation in plants generally shows a negative correlation with carbon chain length, root accumulation has a relatively weaker correlation with high levels of accumulation for both short-chain and long-chain PFAS. In contrast, above-ground tissues (particularly leaves) preferentially accumulate short-chain PFAS. These findings could provide valuable insights into the development of management and mitigation strategies to minimize PFAS accumulation in food crops and subsequently human exposure through the food chain.

title: Manganese Oxides Incubated in Acidic Forest Soil Retain More Organic Carbon Than Iron Oxides
abstract: Abstract Iron (oxyhydr)oxides are well-recognized contributors to soil carbon (C) storage, but the effects of manganese oxides on carbon storage and transformation are relatively unexplored. Here, the relative capacities of Fe and Mn oxides to bind and stabilize soil organic C were directly compared using an in situ incubation experiment. Quartz sands coated with either poorly crystalline Mn(III/IV) oxides or Fe(III) oxides, or left uncoated, were buried in a temperate forest soil for up to one year. Chemical extractions, X-ray absorption and photon spectroscopies, scanning electron microscopy, and neutron scattering were used to evaluate organic and mineral associations and transformations during the incubation. At the end of the 1-year study, Mn oxide stored ∼11× more carbon (42.0 ± 14.3 mg C/m2 oxide) than Fe oxide (3.72 ± 0.37 mg C/m2 oxide) per unit surface area. Manganese oxidation state changed over time, likely reflecting reactions between organic C and Mn oxide, while Fe oxidation state remained unaltered. Total organic C that was associated with Mn oxide was relatively enriched in carboxylic and O-alkyl-C compared to Fe oxides and quartz, either due to preferential sorption or oxidation on the mineral surface. Mn oxides also sorbed high amounts of Ca despite being incubated in an acidic, base-cation depleted soil, which potentially facilitated C sorption. Our study demonstrates that Mn oxides, with the assistance of Ca-bridging, have a greater potential to stabilize organic C than Fe oxides in acidic environments despite higher reactivity.

title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Ecological and Structural Drivers Underlying Species-Specific Estrogen Receptor α Responses to Estrogenic Chemicals in Mammals
abstract: Abstract Species-specific sensitivity to estrogenic chemicals complicates cross-species extrapolation in environmental risk assessment, yet its mechanistic basis remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how ecological traits and amino acid variations in estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) mediate responses to estrogenic chemicals across mammals using an integrated New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) framework combining bioinformatics, in silico structural modeling, machine learning (ML), and in vitro transactivation assays. Two-way clustering of 169 mammalian ERα sequences and 107 ecological traits revealed distinct groupings associated with diet, habitat, and reproductive strategies. Homology model analysis showed that omnivorous species tend to possess larger ligand-binding pockets than carnivores and herbivores. In vitro assays of ERα from six mammalian species demonstrated substantial interspecies variability in response to natural and synthetic estrogenic chemicals. A cetacean-specific substitution from Asn to Ser at position 349 (corresponding to Asn349 in human ERα), which alters hydrogen bonding with Tyr537 in helix-12, was associated with aquatic lifestyles and altered receptor responsiveness. Additionally, ML models identified brain-to-body mass ratio as a candidate predictor of ERα-ligand binding domain sequence variation and ERα-mediated in vitro transactivation sensitivity across species. These findings identify ecological and structural drivers of species-specific estrogen sensitivity and provide a mechanistic framework for improving cross-species prediction of chemical effects in environmental risk assessment.

title: Accounting for Forest Carbon Loss from Natural Gas Development in a Major U.S. Gas Region
abstract: Abstract Natural gas development in forested landscapes can cause substantial forest disturbance, yet its impacts on forest carbon remain poorly quantified. In the Appalachian Basin of the United States, where natural gas production is expected to continue expanding in the coming decades, understanding these impacts is important for evaluating trade-offs between energy production and forest ecosystem services. Here, we combine nationwide forest inventory and remotely sensed data within a Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling framework to quantify forest disturbance, carbon loss, and opportunity cost associated with natural gas development between 2008 and 2021. Using permitted well locations in Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia, we generate pixel-level estimates with associated uncertainty and aggregate results to characterize regional patterns. We estimate that 10 854 ha of forest land were disturbed, resulting in 542 675 (±4275) Mg of forest carbon loss and an opportunity cost of 575 246 (±30 774) Mg of carbon (equivalent to the annual emissions of approximately 464 000 and 492 000 gasoline-powered passenger vehicles, respectively). Disturbance rates were greatest in northern West Virginia, while opportunity costs were highest in northeastern Pennsylvania. To our knowledge, this study provides the first regional-scale quantification of forest carbon loss associated with natural gas development in the Appalachian Basin. The results demonstrate the importance of accounting for forest carbon impacts when evaluating energy development and provide information needed to support future mitigation, planning, and optimization efforts.

title: Dynamics and Controls of Microbial Hydrogen Consumption in Porous Media
abstract: Abstract While nuclear energy contributes significantly to the global energy supply, the long-term management of radioactive waste remains challenging. Deep geological repositories, in which the waste is buried within a low-permeability host rock, are considered the safest storage option. However, hydrogen gas (H2) generated by steel container corrosion may accumulate and create an overpressure that threatens host rock integrity. Access tunnels will be filled with gas-permeable material (such as a sand-bentonite mixture) that mechanically lowers pressure by gas diffusion, but microbial H2 consumption is key to enhancing safety and cost-effectiveness. Hydrogenotrophy is well established in deep subsurface sulfate-reducing bacteria, whereas the activity of other hydrogenotrophs under H2-replete conditions remains poorly constrained. This study examines microbial H2 consumption under repository-relevant conditions in partially saturated sand-bentonite exposed to elevated H2 concentrations. Over 3 months, continuous gas composition and pressure monitoring showed rapid H2 depletion driven by its microbial oxidation coupled to sulfate reduction, methanogenesis, and iron reduction. Water saturation and electron acceptor availability strongly controlled H2 consumption rates. These results clarify the constraints on microbial H2 oxidation in deep geological repositories and inform safety assessments related to gas-induced overpressure.

title: Dynamic Self-Enhancing Proton Interface of Oxyhydroxides Unlocks Concerted Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer for Streamlined Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO3RR) to ammonia (NH3) offers a sustainable route for simultaneous environmental remediation and resource recovery, yet it is fundamentally impeded by sluggish proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) due to diffusion-limited proton delivery, thereby severely undermining the Faradaic efficiency and NH3 selectivity. Here, we exploit a cathodically induced alkaline reconstruction strategy to engineer an intrinsic proton-donating CoOOH/NiOOH interface from a bimetallic Co,Ni precursor on copper foam under NO3RR conditions. The reconstructed CoOOH/NiOOH interface, enriched with dense and labile lattice hydroxyls, functions as a localized solid-state proton donor that spontaneously supplies protons through reversible deprotonation. Crucially, this proton-donating behavior is not static but enters a self-enhancing cycle in which nitrate reduction further accelerates the proton dissociation kinetics, creating a positive feedback loop that continuously amplifies the local generation of reactive hydrogen species. Such a unique mechanism achieves rapid and sustained proton delivery, synchronized with electron transfer that is facilitated by the optimized spin state of the metal centers. The resultant concerted PCET streamlines the reaction pathway of the NO3RR to NH3, bypassing unstable intermediates such as *NH2OH and *H2NO, while suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Consequently, the CoOOH/NiOOH interface exhibits near-unity ammonia selectivity with a Faradaic efficiency exceeding 98% at high nitrate conversion. We further extend this self-enhancing proton interface to bridge nitrate reduction with poly(lactic acid) depolymerization, directly electrosynthesizing alanine and highlighting the potential for dual waste valorization.

title: Machine Learning-Accelerated Advancements in Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
abstract: Abstract With growing concerns over climate change, electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR) has attracted significant attention for converting CO2 into valuable products under mild conditions, but catalyst design remains challenging because traditional, experiment-driven approaches are inefficient and time-consuming. Recently, machine learning (ML), as an advanced data-driven technology, has been widely applied to catalyst design and performance prediction, providing new approaches for rapid screening, structural optimization, and mechanistic exploration of catalysts. Building on these recent advances, this review summarizes the latest applications of ML in CO2RR technology, focusing on ML applications in catalyst performance prediction, key descriptor discovery, catalyst screening, mechanistic investigation, and optimization of synthesis parameters. Additionally, this review discusses the challenges faced by ML in CO2RR catalyst development, including data scarcity, poor model generalization, and difficulties in multiobjective optimization, while looking ahead to future directions such as transfer learning, the establishment of automated synthesis platforms, and the integration of multiobjective optimization frameworks, thereby providing a roadmap for the rational design of next-generation CO2RR catalysts that aims to guide the development of data-driven catalyst design approach.

title: Near-Quantitative Electrochemical Upcycling of Halonitrobenzenes in Wastewater to Valuable Haloanilines over Facet-Engineered Copper Catalysts
abstract: Abstract Selective electrocatalytic hydrogenation of halonitrobenzenes (HNBs) in wastewater to value-added haloanilines (HANs) offers a sustainable strategy for simultaneous pollutant abatement and resource recovery. However, achieving high HANs selectivity under ambient conditions remains challenging. Here we report a facet-engineered Cu electrocatalyst that enables selective hydrogenation of HNBs to HANs. Using p-chloronitrobenzene (p-CNB) as a model pollutant, the Cu catalyst achieves complete p-CNB removal with a 98.9% p-chloroaniline (p-CAN) selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the outstanding performance of Cu originates from an optimal balance between moderate H* generation and facile desorption of the p-CAN product, which promotes efficient −NO2 to −NH2 reduction while effectively suppressing the over-dechlorination of p-CAN. Furthermore, it is found that the Cu(111) facet is intrinsically more active than Cu(200) and Cu(220), attributable to its higher p-CAN desorption ability. Guided by these insights, a Cu(111)-enriched electrode is rationally engineered, exhibiting an ultrahigh Faradaic efficiency of 99.4%. Finally, a tandem device integrating an electrolyzer and an extraction-distillation separation unit is developed, enabling the efficient recovery of high-purity p-CAN product. This study demonstrates a sustainable electrochemical pathway for converting hazardous pollutants into valuable chemicals, advancing low-carbon wastewater treatment and resource recovery.

title: What Are the Sources of Unclassified Organosulfates in the Atmosphere?
abstract: Abstract Organosulfates (OSs) are ubiquitous components of atmospheric aerosols, contributing up to 30% of total aerosol mass, yet their sources remain poorly constrained. Recently, we have compiled 366 ambient OS molecular formulas from previous field studies and found that only about 36% can be assigned to known precursors or formation mechanisms. These mechanisms primarily explain the production of freshly formed OSs via photochemical and/or condensed-phase reactions associated with different precursors. Consequently, 64% of observed OS formulas remain unclassified. Concurrently, laboratory studies have revealed that certain OSs can undergo efficient multiphase transformation through heterogeneous and aqueous-phase reactions, yielding higher-generation OS products. Although such studies are still limited, the identified transformation OS products can account for about 17% of all reported ambient OS formulas and, notably, explain an additional 5% of previously unclassified OS signals. These findings imply that a potential fraction of ambient OSs may not be freshly formed but rather secondary or higher-generation products arising from chemical transformation. Current field analyses and atmospheric models focus mostly on precursor-specific OS formation pathways, largely overlooking the role of OS transformation. We therefore propose that transformation of freshly formed OSs is an important and previously underrecognized source of unclassified ambient OSs.

title: Multisource Observation-Constrained Tuning for Air Quality Forecasting in a Machine Learning-Enhanced NOAA Unified Forecast System
abstract: Abstract Accurate near-real-time (NRT) air quality forecasting is critical for protecting public health but remains challenged by uncertainties in emissions, meteorology, and initial conditions within traditional chemical transport models (CTMs). We present an observation-driven machine learning framework that integrates multisource satellite products, including VIIRS aerosol optical depth and TEMPO NO2 with U.S. EPA AirNow measurements into a machine-learning surrogate of the NOAA Unified Forecast System (DeepAQM). A ConvLSTM-ResNet fusion module reconstructs spatially continuous surface PM2.5 and O3 fields from sparse observations, providing updated initial conditions for 72 h forecasts across the continental United States. DeepAQM reproduces UFS-AQM spatial patterns with strong agreement (R2 > 0.9 for O3 and up to 0.80 for PM2.5) while maintaining normalized mean bias within ±10%. Observation-updated initial conditions improve early forecast skill, increasing site-level R2 during the first 10 forecast hours from approximately 0.10–0.15 to 0.40–0.50 for PM2.5 and from approximately 0.40 to 0.50 for O3. Observation-based fine-tuning provides additional improvements throughout the 72 h forecast period, increasing overall R2 to 0.41 for PM2.5 and 0.82 for O3 during the independent evaluation period. These results demonstrate that integrating satellite and ground observations within DeepAQM can enhance NRT air quality forecasting and provide a scalable pathway toward globally deployable observation-driven prediction systems.

title: Prioritizing and Grouping Food Contact Chemicals: From Chaos to Clarity
abstract: Abstract At least 2,160 food contact chemicals (FCCs) are known to migrate into foodstuffs, and some of them, such as certain bisphenols and ortho-phthalates, have been partially regulated in a few geographic regions due to health risks. However, the current approach to chemicals management is slow and can lead to regrettable substitutions, as seen with bisphenol A (BPA, CAS 80-05-7) being replaced by bisphenol S (BPS, CAS 80-09-1). To help address these issues and provide evidence-based guidance, we systematically prioritized the currently known 15,159 FCCs based on their well-known human health hazards and exposure potential from food contact materials (FCMs). Overall, 1,222 FCCs make up the FCCprio List. These FCCs are carcinogenic, mutagenic, toxic for reproduction, toxic for specific target organs, endocrine disrupting, persistent, bioaccumulative, and/or mobile, based on GHS-aligned hazard data. 94 FCCs are assigned to the highest tier (Tier 1) because of evidence for migration into food and presence in humans from human biomonitoring programs. We then grouped all known FCCs by chemical structure and identified 38 priority structural groups with a particularly high fraction of known hazardous chemicals, including well-known priority groups such as ortho-phthalates and PFASs as well as less-discussed groups (e.g., primary aromatic amines, organophosphates, isocyanates). Importantly, 4,222 FCCs fall into priority groups, meaning they are structurally closely related to hazardous FCCs, and 70% of these FCCs lack adequate hazard data─indicating significant knowledge gaps and the potential for regrettable substitutions. While these results highlight potential for prioritizing data-poor FCCs through grouping, ultimately more holistic strategies, including mixture toxicity assessment or testing finished FCMs for biological activity, are needed to reduce the overall human exposure to hazardous or untested FCCs migrating from FCMs.

title: Fatty Acid-Derived Metabolic Indicators and Biomagnification of Halogenated Organic Contaminants: A Comparative Analysis of Adjacent Coastal Predator-Based Food Webs
abstract: Abstract Fatty acids (FAs) mediate trophic energy transfer and may reflect biochemical responses to contaminant exposure, yet their linkage with halogenated organic contaminants (HOCs) across adjacent coastal food webs remains unclear. This study comparatively examined the occurrence, biomagnification, and associations between 103 HOCs and 36 FAs in two predator-based food webs from the Pearl River Estuary: a marine fish–dolphin (Sousa chinensis) food web and a mangrove-associated terrestrial insect–spider (Nephila pilipes) food web. The fish–dolphin food web exhibited higher HOC biomagnification (BMFs < 489) and trophic magnification (TMFs < 5.19) than the insect–spider food web (BMFs < 2.78; TMFs < 3.08), although both showed similar biomagnification peaks at log KOW ≈ 7 and log KOA ≈ 11. Multivariate analyses identified 2,2′,4,4′,5,5′-hexachlorobiphenyl (PCB-153), 2,2′,4,4′-tetrabromodiphenyl ether (BDE-47), and a medium-chain chlorinated paraffin congener (C17H29Cl7) as contaminants most strongly associated with dolphin FA profiles, whereas 2-ethylhexyl-2,3,4,5-tetrabromobenzoate (TBB), bis(2-ethylhexyl)-tetrabromophthalate (TBPH), and 1,1,1-trichloro-2,2-bis(4-chlorophenyl)ethane (p,p′-DDT) were predominant contributors in spiders. HOC concentrations showed positive associations with saturated FAs in dolphins but negative associations with polyunsaturated FAs in spiders, and were significantly associated with FA-derived metabolic indices (R2 = 0.234–0.554, p < 0.05), including stearoyl-CoA desaturase 16 (SCD16) and stearoyl-CoA desaturase 18 (SCD18) in dolphins, and delta-6-desaturase (D6D) and de novo lipogenesis (DNL) in spiders. These relationships are correlative and likely reflect the combined influence of food-web characteristics, contaminant exposure, and species-specific physiology. This study provides a comparative assessment of HOC biomagnification and FA-derived metabolic indicators across contrasting predator-based coastal food webs.

title: Expanding the Scope of PFAS Research to Include Adipose Tissues
abstract: Abstract The occurrence and burden of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in adipose tissue of humans and wildlife represent an underexamined dimension of PFAS exposure. While most PFAS research has focused on ionic substances that accumulate in tissues such as liver and blood, there is growing evidence that a distinct and diverse suite of neutral PFAS bioaccumulate in adipose tissue. This Perspective synthesizes recent data illustrating the substantial contribution of some adipose-associated PFAS to overall body burdens, applies quantum chemical modeling to exemplify additional PFAS likely to partition into adipose tissue, and examines analytical blindspots that have limited their detection to date. We show that certain neutral PFAS possess partitioning properties comparable to legacy persistent organic pollutants, which, provided that they are sufficiently persistent, can lead to bioaccumulation in adipose tissue. We further outline the analytical challenge of extracting, detecting, and quantifying neutral PFAS in matrices rich in storage lipids and discuss the implications for exposure assessment, toxicology, and environmental surveillance. Finally, we identify key research needs and call for expanded monitoring strategies that capture the full chemical space of PFAS bioaccumulation.

title: Associations between Prenatal Exposure to Perchlorate, Thiocyanate, and Nitrate and Child Neurodevelopment in the MARBLES Study
abstract: Abstract Associations between prenatal exposure to perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remain largely unexplored. We investigated these associations in the MARBLES cohort, a prospective cohort with an elevated familial likelihood of ASD. A total of 310 mothers provided 1916 urine samples during pregnancy, and their children were classified at age 3 years as typically developing (TD), ASD, or non-TD (developmental concerns not meeting ASD diagnostic criteria). We estimated relative risks for ASD and non-TD compared with TD using Poisson regression and assessed mixture effects using quantile G-computation and Bayesian kernel machine regression. Overall and mixture analyses showed no significant associations between prenatal exposure to these NIS inhibitors and the child neurodevelopmental outcomes. However, stratified analyses identified several context-specific associations according to child sex, trimester of exposure, maternal urinary iodine concentration, and passive smoking status, some of which remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. These findings suggest that susceptibility to prenatal exposure to perchlorate, thiocyanate, and nitrate may vary across population subgroups and exposure windows. Although these subgroup-specific associations should be considered hypothesis generating, they highlight the need for future studies integrating thyroid biomarkers and mechanistic approaches to better understand thyroid-related pathways underlying child neurodevelopment.

title: In situ Simultaneous Removal of Fe(II), Mn(II), and NH4+-N from Groundwater by Codosing of Peroxymonosulfate and Trace HClO: Mechanism and 3D Tank Experiment
abstract: Abstract NH4+-N, Fe(II), and Mn(II), common coexisting components in native poor-quality groundwater, were targeted in this study using a simultaneous removal strategy that involved codosing of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and trace HClO. Unlike traditional HClO-catalyzed Mn(II) oxidation, rapid iron oxides formation bypassed the slow homogeneous catalytic phase, enabling faster electron transfer between the more reactive PMS and Mn(II) adsorbed on iron oxides. The resulting iron–manganese oxides not only removed Fe(II) and Mn(II) but also shifted PMS activation from homogeneous (driven by free Fe(II)) to heterogeneous catalysis, overcoming limitations from low Fe(II) levels in groundwater. Their amorphous structure enhanced PMS adsorption, while bimetallic Fe–Mn sites supported redox cycling among Mn(IV)/Mn(III)/Mn(II)(s) and Fe(III)/Fe(II)(s), sustaining PMS activation and SO4•– generation. HClO participated directly in SO4•–-initiated chain reactions, boosting ClO• concentration by 102-fold. ClO• dominated ammonium removal─especially surface-enriched NH4+ -N─selectively converting it to N2 (>88%). Three-dimensional sand tank experiments evaluated lateral, radial, and vertical reagent percolation and in situ remediation efficiency in heterogeneous aquifers through optimized monitoring wells, injection screen lengths, and hydraulic gradient control. This study advances in situ groundwater remediation technology, offering lab-scale mechanistic insights and experimental validation.

title: High-Resolution Assessment of Terrestrial Carbon Storage and Restoration Benefits in China, 1990–2023
abstract: Abstract Terrestrial ecosystems serve as critical carbon sinks, playing an important role in the global carbon cycle and climate regulation. However, previous estimates of carbon storage in China’s terrestrial ecosystems remain uncertain due to variability in data sources and methodological approaches. This study integrates multisource remote sensing data with extensive field-sampling data sets of carbon density, leveraging machine learning models to provide a comprehensive estimation of multiyear carbon storage and annual dynamics across multiple carbon pools. We estimated project-region carbon-stock changes using a scenario-based accounting framework. The total carbon storage, encompassing vegetation biomass and soil organic carbon, is estimated at 113.48 Pg C, with 20.4% in vegetation biomass and 79.6% in soil. Across land-use types, forests store the largest share, with 47.99 Pg C, followed by grasslands, croplands, barren lands, shrublands, and wetlands, which stored 32.32, 18.00, 14.65, 0.49, and 0.02 Pg C, respectively. National carbon stocks fluctuated over the study period but increased by 6.62 Pg C from 2014 to 2023. Scenario-based accounting indicates an additional baseline-adjusted project-region carbon-stock gain of 0.495 Pg C within major restoration regions during 2014–2023, equivalent to 0.050 Pg C yr–1. These results provide a high-resolution reconstruction of China’s terrestrial carbon stocks and clarify recent carbon-stock changes across ecosystems, regions, and major restoration areas.

title: Polystyrene Microplastics Exacerbate Arsenic-Induced Ferroptosis and Lipid Metabolism Dysregulation in Chicken Hepatocytes through SIRT7-SIRT1 Axis-Associated Transcriptomic Alterations
abstract: Abstract Co-contamination with arsenic (As) and polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) poses a significant risk to environmental health. This study elucidated the synergistic toxicity mechanism of PS-MPs and As using a chicken hepatocyte model, integrating electron microscopy, migration assays, and comprehensive biomarker assessment. Toxicity prediction, molecular docking, transcriptomics, protein–protein interaction networks, and Pearson correlation analysis were further employed to clarify the underlying mechanism of their combined toxic effects. Molecular docking analysis provided supporting computational evidence that the styrene monomer derived from PS-MPs interferes with antioxidant proteins (e.g., SIRT1), suggesting a possible mechanism by which PS-MPs could exacerbate intracellular As accumulation. This interaction precipitates a vicious cycle of oxidative stress and lipid metabolism disorders. Further research has found that synergistic toxicity was significantly associated with a coordinated dysregulation of SIRT7 and SIRT1, suggesting a perturbation of the dynamic balance between these two regulators. This imbalance subsequently suppresses PPAR-α signaling and GPX4, while upregulating lipid accumulation markers and ferroptosis drivers such as ACSL4. These findings, together with functional validation via SIRT1 overexpression and SIRT7 knockdown, identify a potential core regulatory axis of the SIRT7-SIRT1 protein network in the synergistic toxicity of As-PS-MPs. Our research provides a new framework for the toxicological analysis of PS-MPs and As through transcriptomics and bioinformatics analysis and offers new ideas for further studies on combined pollutant exposure.

title: From Detection toward Mitigation: A Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Methane Emissions Reduction
abstract: Abstract Methane is a potent greenhouse gas and a major contributor to near-term climate warming, yet emissions remain difficult to detect, quantify, and mitigate because they are spatially heterogeneous, temporally intermittent, and shaped by sector-specific measurement constraints. This review critically assesses artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) for methane monitoring and the translation of monitoring toward mitigation by synthesizing 63 studies published between 2018 and 2025, from which 93 model instances were coded across energy, agriculture/livestock, and waste management applications. We compare tree-based ensembles, classical machine learning methods, convolutional and recurrent neural networks, transformers, and hybrid/physics-guided architectures through a decision-oriented lens: data availability, validation type, uncertainty treatment, transferability, and operational relevance. Tree-based models remain attractive for structured predictors and interpretable driver ranking; deep learning dominates image- and video-based plume detection; and hybrid models are most useful when they fuse complementary sensors or enforce transport constraints. Across the reviewed evidence, AI/ML is most credible for screening and ranking large, persistent sources, while generalizable quantification of smaller, intermittent, or diffuse sources remains limited by wind uncertainty, small or proprietary training data sets, inconsistent metrics, and limited cross-region validation. Priorities for advancing AI-enabled methane mitigation include sector- and platform-specific benchmarks, calibrated uncertainty, physics-informed learning, explicit decision-support rules, and pilot demonstrations that measure avoided emissions rather than model accuracy alone.

title: Aerosol-Assisted Metal Poisoning of Cu/SSZ-13 during NH 3 -SCR Operation
abstract: Abstract Cu/SSZ-13 is a benchmark catalyst for the selective catalytic reduction (SCR) of NOx with NH3 in diesel exhaust aftertreatment, but its activity can be severely impaired by alkali and alkaline-earth metal poisoning. Conventional impregnation of catalysts with such poisons involves introducing metal species prior to catalytic testing. This means that any poisoning that develops concurrently with catalyst operation is not captured. Here, we develop an aerosol-assisted, reaction-coupled poisoning platform that continuously delivers metal-containing aqueous aerosols to SCR catalysts under hydrated NH3–SCR conditions. At nearly identical K loadings, aerosol-assisted poisoning caused substantially greater deactivation of Cu/SSZ-13 than conventional impregnation of the catalyst, with a more pronounced activity loss after poisoning at 400 °C than at 200 °C. The enhanced deactivation was accompanied by a more spatially extensive K distribution, stronger perturbations of the zeolite framework, preferential alteration of 8-membered-ring-associated [Cu(OH)]+–Z species, spectroscopic signatures consistent with CuOx aggregation, and partial neutralization of Brønsted acid sites. Similar pathway- and temperature-dependent deactivation trends were observed for Na-, Mg-, and Ca-poisoned Cu/SSZ-13 and for K-poisoned V2O5–WO3/TiO2. These results establish aerosol-assisted poisoning as a controlled, accelerated approach for evaluating metal-induced deactivation of SCR catalysts under hydrated reaction conditions.

title: Sludge-derived biochar-activated peroxymonosulfate as a waste-to-resource pretreatment for sustainable membrane fouling control: Adsorption-oxidation interplay and thermodynamic insights
Are environmental standards unsustainable? A discussion through the regulatory uncertainty of double materiality
abstract: Although environmental standards are intended to support ecological transition, the regulatory uncertainty surrounding their implementation may paradoxically reinforce the neoliberal logics of the very financial capitalism they claim to challenge. This article examines to what extent, and through which mechanisms, the uncertainty associated with double materiality transforms environmental reporting mechanisms into (counter-)performative tools. We analyse 812 CSR reports issued between 2016 and 2022 by the largest French listed firms (SBF120). Using a structured content analysis, we identify four reporting profiles and show a marked phase of instability between 2017 and 2019, during which time dominant firms in the field test and recombine registers of legitimation while concrete requirements remain unclear. Our results suggest that uncertainty is not merely an obstacle to compliance, but can become a strategic lever through which dominant actors reappropriate the (critical) language embedded in emerging sustainability standards, prioritise communication over action, and produce symbolic reports. In this sense, double materiality risks operating as a counter-performative standard, enabling reporting to be deployed as an instrument of legitimation that renews and reinforces neoliberal logics, potentially to the benefit of the most polluting firms. We thus expand the debate on the political role of quantification mechanisms and underscore the need to rethink the institutional and political conditions under which double materiality can become a genuine lever for environmental change rather than a language that fuels the capitalist machine.

title: Rubberized Engineered/Strain-Hardening Geopolymer Composites (EGC/SHGC) with low fiber content to enhance strength and ductility efficiencies
Machine learning-based integration of plant growth regulators and overcompensation enhances microalgal protein production from wastewater
abstract: Photoautotrophic wastewater valorization represents a sustainable route for carbon-neutral nutrient upcycling into bioproducts. However, its practical implementation is often constrained by wastewater-induced growth inhibition. Besides, the distribution of metabolic flux across competing pathways may further restrict nutrient allocation towards target product. In this study, we propose a combined strategy integrating plant growth regulators (PGRs) with a nitrogen overcompensation strategy to enhance microalgal performance during potato starch wastewater treatment. Gibberellic acid (GA 3 ) and naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) both alleviated wastewater inhibition and enhanced nutrient recovery in Chlorella pyrenoidosa , achieving up to 79.9% total nitrogen removal. Notably, supplementation with 10 mg L −1 GA 3 resulted in a 26.2% increase in biomass compared to controls. The random forest model identified candidate high-response concentrations of approximately 10.5 ± 1 mg L −1 for GA 3 and 10.2 ± 1 mg L −1 for NAA and suggested declining biomass responses at higher NAA concentrations, whereas GA 3 showed a broader model-predicted growth-promoting range. Under the nitrogen starvation–repletion condition, PGR-supplemented cultures achieved maximum biomass and protein concentrations of up to 1.58 g L −1 and 594.82 mg L −1 , respectively, together with over 90% removal of COD, total phosphorus, and ammonium. Transcriptomic profiling indicated that GA 3 induced significant upregulation of genes involved in photosynthetic apparatus function, ribosomal biogenesis, and transmembrane transport processes compared to NAA. This work establishes a strategy that integrates PGRs with nitrogen overcompensation to overcome wastewater-induced stress. The proposed approach provides a practical strategy for improving microalgal productivity and nutrient recovery from high-strength wastewater, advancing the development of carbon-neutral biorefinery systems.

Techno–economic optimisation of hydrogen geological storage in UK depleted gas reservoirs
abstract: Long-duration energy storage is becoming critical in the UK to manage renewable intermittency, prolonged low-generation periods, and energy curtailment. Depleted natural gas reservoirs offer a promising option for large-scale underground hydrogen storage because of their substantial capacities, established containment, and well-characterised geology. However, a systematic assessment linking reservoir-scale behaviour to cost-optimal UK storage portfolios remains lacking. Here, we formulate a cost-aware portfolio optimisation framework that combines compositional reservoir simulations, surrogate modelling, and techno-economic optimisation across representative UK reservoir properties and operating conditions. The simulations identify permeability, porosity, reservoir pressure, and density contrast between H 2 and cushion gas as the dominant controls on recovery, while injection rate and cycle duration have comparatively lower influence. These results support a high-accuracy surrogate model that enables rapid evaluation of feasible storage configurations for delivery requirements from 5 to 200 TWh. By linking reservoir-dependent recovery to H 2 losses, purification, and storage-system costs, the framework determines cost-optimal combinations of depleted gas reservoirs and operating strategies. The optimised portfolios produce long-term levelised storage costs of approximately 30–60 $ MWh −1 . Higher delivery requirements generally increase costs because fewer annual cycles are available to distribute infrastructure and inventory costs. When purification costs approach H 2 production costs, cushion-gas ratios of 2–4 are favoured for the 5 TWh case, decreasing to 0–1 for requirements of 100 TWh and above; inexpensive purification shifts the preferred ratio towards zero. Across scenarios, selected reservoirs consistently exhibit permeabilities of 10–30 mD, porosities of 0.10–0.15, and pressures of 250–300 bar, conditions that reduce buoyant mixing while maintaining practical deliverability.

title: Thermodynamic performance’s analysis of a hybrid thermal-compressor-thermochemical sorption processes using ammoniated salts for cold production
Disentangling the effects of dung pat shape and mass on greenhouse gas emissions in the presence of dung beetles
abstract: Dung beetles (Coleoptera: Scarabaeoidea) can influence greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) from pasture systems by altering dung decomposition processes. However, the magnitude and direction of the effect of dung beetle presence on dung GHG emissions are not consistent across studies, potentially due to variations in experimental practices. To better understand dung beetles' emission mitigation potential, this study seeks to evaluate how the interactions between dung shape, mass, and dung beetle presence affect dung GHG emissions. A laboratory experiment was conducted to assess the effects of Onthophagus nuchicornis presence, dung shape, and dung mass on dairy cattle dung GHG emissions over a 21-day period. Results revealed that dung mass can significantly impact the effect of dung beetle presence on dung CO 2 emissions. The presence of dung beetles in mesocosms containing 100 g dung pats increased CO 2 emissions by 29%, while their presence in mesocosms containing the 400 g dung pats increased emissions by 64%. Additionally, the interaction between dung shape and mass, as well as dung shape and beetle presence significantly impacted CH 4 emissions. Flattening 100 g dung pats resulted in a 44% reduction in CH 4 emissions, while flattening 400 g dung pats reduced CH 4 emissions by 13%. Beetle presence in flattened dung pats resulted in a 72% reduction in CH 4 emissions, whereas their presence in non-flattened dung pats only resulted in an 8% reduction in CH 4 emissions. These findings reveal the importance of methodological decisions when studying the relationship between dung beetle activity and GHG emissions from dung pats.

title: Geogenic CO2 emissions from post-mining landscapes: Environmental and public health implications in rapidly urbanizing zones of Jos, North central Nigeria
Supply-system-level aggregation of structurally constrained mineral resources: A framework for vein graphite
abstract: Vein graphite deposits contain exceptionally high-purity graphite but remain minor contributors to global supply because their narrow, discontinuous, and structurally controlled geometry limits conventional approaches to scaling production. This paper argues that the principal constraint on vein graphite development is not resource quality, but supply-system design. Using vein graphite as a case study, a supply-system-level aggregation framework is proposed in which multiple distributed mining operations are integrated through centralized processing, quality management, logistics, and traceability systems. The framework demonstrates how coordination across operations can transform fragmented production into consistent, specification-compliant supply capable of meeting modern market requirements. The analysis further examines governance, market access, resource integration, and circular economy considerations that influence implementation. While developed for vein graphite, the framework is applicable to a broader class of structurally constrained and distributed mineral resources. The results suggest that supply-chain participation increasingly depends on supply-system integration and institutional coordination as much as on geological endowment.

title: Limits of policy: Local content and resource curse dynamics - evidence from Guyana
abstract: Guyana's 2021 Local Content Act is among the Caribbean's most ambitious efforts to ensure that newly discovered oil wealth generates broad-based domestic economic participation. Using synthetic control methods to construct counterfactuals from structurally comparable economies, this study examines the macroeconomic trajectory of Guyana after the implementation of the local content Act during an active oil boom. The results reveal that while Guyana achieved substantial post-2021 income gains relative to its counterfactual, these gains were accompanied by pronounced structural pressures. Specifically, estimates indicate a contraction in the share of manufacturing value-added and an appreciation of the real effective exchange rate associated with the post-2021 period. These findings suggest that local content mandate is insufficient to offset structural pressures associated with the boom itself.

Rainfall‐Induced Physical Crusting Is Associated With Near‐Surface Structural Degradation and Strain Localization During Drying in Loess Soil
abstract: ABSTRACT Rainfall‐induced physical crusting is associated with degradation of near‐surface soil structure, but its pore‐scale structural and mechanical evolution during drying remains poorly resolved. We combined time‐resolved X‐ray computed tomography (XCT), digital volume correlation (DVC), and surface‐aligned stratification to track pore architecture and internal strain in loess soil cores subjected to different antecedent rainfall durations. Surface‐aligned porosity profiles identified a compacted zone within the upper few millimeters, supporting comparison of a 0–3 mm shell with a 3–10 mm subsurface band. Within the shell, rainfall‐treated cores had mean total porosity approximately 24% lower than CK at 0 h and 46% lower at the final dry state. Pore‐network analysis showed mean coordination numbers approximately 24% lower through 108 h and 32% lower at the final state, while pore and throat sizes varied among stages. Across rainfall‐treated cores, mean first principal strain was 0.025 in the 0–2.4 mm band and 0.002 in the 3.6–9.6 mm band; the near‐surface mean was also descriptively higher than in CK (0.004), and every rainfall‐treated core mean exceeded both CK core means. Together, these observations show that rainfall‐induced crusting is associated with a near‐surface structural degradation pattern in which pore‐network fragmentation and tensile‐strain localization develop within the same operational depth domain during drying. Under the tested laboratory conditions, this layer‐resolved evidence supports interpreting rainfall‐induced physical crusting not only as a thin surface morphology but also as an evolving near‐surface structural degradation process during drying.

title: Post‐Fire Soil Organic Carbon Dynamics: Decline and Recovery Over Two Decades
abstract: ABSTRACT Wildfire can significantly alter soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics in forest ecosystems, with complex temporal patterns following fire events. However, research on post‐fire SOC recovery remains limited, particularly in dry‐warm valley regions that are prone to frequent forest fires. This study, based on field investigations and experimental analyses, focused on severely burned sites in the dry‐warm valley of Anning River Basin, Hengduan Mountainous Region, China, from 1996 to 2021. The space‐for‐time substitution method was employed to reveal the patterns of SOC changes in burned sites at different recovery stages and explore influencing factors on SOC. The results showed that SOC and its components were significantly negatively correlated with soil depth and slope aspect ( p < 0.05) but significantly positively correlated with time since fire ( p < 0.01). Specifically, SOC, readily oxidizable carbon (ROC), non‐labile organic carbon (NLOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), and mineral‐associated organic carbon (MOC) decreased with the increase in soil depth, with higher content on shady slopes compared with sunny slopes for burned sites and unburned sites. Over a 26‐year recovery timeline, SOC and its components in severely burned sites exhibited an initial decline followed by a gradual increase, with the decline commencing approximately five years after the fire. During the first 10 years of natural recovery, SOC, ROC, NLOC, POC, and MOC contents decreased but thereafter started to increase, while POC content began to increase after 20 years of recovery. Soil physicochemical properties, including soil pH and bulk density, were significantly negatively correlated with SOC and its components ( p < 0.01). Soil porosity, clay, fine root biomass, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and cation exchange capacity exhibited significant positive correlations with SOC and its components ( p < 0.05). ROC, NLOC, POC, and MOC contents were highly positively correlated with SOC content ( p < 0.01). Overall, the findings indicate that SOC loss after severe wildfire can persist for up to a decade, and that full recovery of some SOC components, such as POC, may require over 20 years.

title: Body parts used for ancient Egyptian artworks traced to surprising source
J. Michael Bishop: A remembrance—Not a hagiography
The regulatory logic linking inflammation and fibrosis
abstract: Whether tissue injury resolves or progresses to chronic scarring is determined by regulatory choices that remain only partially understood. In this review, we propose that immune cells and fibroblasts function as dynamic interpreters of intercellular cues, integrating these signals through chromatin-regulated gene circuits that govern cell state and fate. Drawing on insights from cardiac biology and from settings where tissues regenerate or resolve injury without scarring, we outline a molecular framework in which immune-stromal crosstalk and gene regulatory networks dictate the choice between recovery and chronic fibrosis across organs, including the heart, lung, liver, and kidney. Reframing fibrosis as a reversible state shaped by disrupted regulatory logic opens therapeutic avenues that move beyond suppressing fibrotic outputs toward rewiring the regulatory programs that sustain them.

title: Genomics and social practices at Mogou and other Gansu sites during prehistoric trans-Eurasian exchange
abstract: Beginning approximately 4,000 years ago, southwest-Asian-originating domesticated crops and livestock began appearing in Gansu, a key crossroads in northwestern China, yet the population dynamics and social practices underlying these historically transformative events in the region have not been fully explored. Despite the adoption of western domesticates, genome sequences of 149 individuals from the large Mogou cemetery and ten other sites in Gansu, dating between 4,700 and 3,000 years ago, revealed migrations within East Asian regions but no detectable evidence of genetic influence from western or central Eurasia, suggesting that early agricultural dispersals may have followed a model distinct from that documented in Europe and Central Asia. The Mogou cemetery represents a continuous community that interacted with surrounding regions but does not exhibit clear matrilocal or patrilocal residential patterns. We found no strong evidence that co-buried individuals represented biological relatives. Non-local ancestry appears to be linked to lower-status burial practices.

title: Metabolite buffering of labile iron governs ferroptosis
The organization of visual pathways in the Drosophila brain
Enteric glial serotonin signaling drives anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer
Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
abstract: Sex differences in behavior exist across all animals, typically under strong genetic regulation. In Drosophila , fruitless / doublesex transcription factors identify dimorphic neurons, but their organization into functional circuits remains unclear. We present the connectome of the entire Drosophila male central nervous system. This contains 166,700 neurons spanning the brain and nerve cord, fully proofread and annotated, including fruitless / doublesex expression and 11,710 neuron types. We provide the first comprehensive comparison between male and female brain connectomes to synaptic resolution, finding 8,069 isomorphic, 138 dimorphic, 289 male-specific, and 71 female-specific types. This resource enables analysis of full sensory-to-motor circuits underlying complex behaviors and the impact of dimorphic elements. Sex-specific/dimorphic neurons are concentrated in higher brain centers, while the sensory and motor periphery is largely isomorphic. Within higher centers, male-specific connections are organized into hotspots defined by male-specific neurons or arbors. Dimorphic neurons reroute information across sexes.

title: The complete gustatory connectome of adult Drosophila reveals how taste guides feeding, foraging, and social behavior
Exclusive Secrets,
abstract: Abstract We investigate the effects of trade secret (TS) protection on supplier exclusivity in vertical industrial relations. We show that manufacturers limit their suppliers’ buyer networks under weak TS protection to safeguard sensitive information while encouraging supplier investment. Using worldwide automotive parts contracts data, we find that weak TS protection constrains suppliers to serve only a few Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), sometimes leading to exclusivity, especially for parts with intermediate relationship-specificity. This association strengthens with greater OEM bargaining power, aligning with theoretical insights. We validate these findings by examining supplier attributes, including size, cartel involvement, and ownership structure. F23, O34, L14, L24, L62

title: Labor unions and deaths of despair: Evidence from right-to-work laws
Designing renewable energy auctions for high realization probability – CfD and payment-only auctions
abstract: In recent years, different instruments for renewable energy expansion have been debated. Among the support and hedging instruments, two-sided contracts for difference (CfDs) have become the default in many countries and are promoted by the European Commission. On the other hand, payment-only auctions have also become established, where the electricity sales are unregulated, but the winners must pay for the right to build energy plants. Focusing on a high realization probability and the induced welfare effects, we compare two-sided CfDs with payment-only auctions. Contrary to the conventional wisdom, the non-realization risk is higher with auctioned CfDs than with payment-only auctions and is exacerbated by risk aversion, when developers can cope with both options. CfDs are particularly useful when developers need support for implementing their projects. Against this backdrop and considering asymmetric information, i.e., developers know best the economic conditions of their projects, we propose a design in which developers decide competitively between a CfD auction and a payment-only auction and which enhances the realization probability.
