title: Perceptions of artificial intelligence bias and gender inclusivity: toward a gendered divergence
Driver-personalized risk assessment in car-following: validation of an optical-flow-based model using SHRP 2 naturalistic driving
Fraternal Birth Order Effect and Other Sibship Effects in Bisexual and Asexual Men and Women
abstract: Abstract Previous research has shown that homosexual men and women tend to have more older brothers than their heterosexual counterparts—this is known as the fraternal birth order effect (FBOE) and is usually considered a marker for biological development of sexual orientation. Recent studies suggest this effect might also apply to bisexual and asexual individuals who have been overlooked by previous scholarship. In this study, I explored associations of the FBOE and other sibship effects with minority sexual orientation in an online collected sample of heterosexual ( n = 1174), bisexual ( n = 432), and asexual ( n = 90) men and women from Czechia and Slovakia. Results of the binary logistic regression indicated the FBOE in bisexual men ( OR = 1.66) but not in other sexual minority groups. There were no significant differences in other sibship characteristics between sexual minority and heterosexual individuals, although other non-heterosexual study groups showed a non-significant FBOE of a magnitude similar to bisexual men. This study contributes to the limited literature on understudied bisexual and asexual populations and indicates that male bisexuality might share a common biodevelopmental origin with male and possibly also female homosexuality.

title: Reform for all? The limits of expertise in producing equitable outcomes
abstract: Administrative reforms often seek to improve performance by changing bureaucratic or professional expertise. Yet technical skills alone may not disrupt the forces that generate unequal outcomes across social groups. We argue that systemic bias shapes professionalization and discretionary judgment, limiting expertise-substitution reforms’ capacity to reduce racial disparities even when they improve average outcomes. We test this using a 2018 Dallas reform that deployed co-response teams pairing police officers with clinicians and social workers on mental health calls. A difference-in-­differences analysis across divisions finds significant reductions in psychiatric holds and arrests, but the gains concentrate among White male citizens; arrests of Black males increase significantly. A complementary incident-level analysis of the conditional probability of a coercive outcome points to a different pattern of heterogeneous effects: White males show a higher post-reform probability of psychiatric holds while Black females and Hispanic males experience lower ones. Both sets of findings shed new light on the scholarship of administrative reform and hold practical implications for both the impact of such programs and the ways in which they are evaluated.

title: Socially oriented contracting and public employees’ job satisfaction: evidence from the federal small disadvantaged business program
abstract: While contracting out is often viewed as having negative consequences for public employees, less attention has been paid to the positive outcomes certain types of contracting may have for them. In particular, recent scholarship proposes that contracting out may improve employees’ work attitudes when it emphasizes pro-social factors in the process. Using the case of the federal Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) contracting program—which emphasizes diversity and equity in procurement—this study examines whether contracting programs that promote social outcomes are associated with public employees’ job satisfaction. Drawing from research on sector differences, person-organization fit, and representative bureaucracy, we hypothesize a positive association between SDB contracting efforts and job satisfaction, with employees from underrepresented backgrounds experiencing a more pronounced increase. Linking U.S. federal government contracting data to the Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey (FEVS), our analyses provide support for the hypotheses. The implications of these findings for government contracting and public human resource management are discussed.

title: Arrested development: how performance regimes constrain changes to public sector performance measurement
abstract: Public sector organizations increasingly operate within broader performance regimes—the wider systems of rules, actors, and practices that shape how performance is measured and managed—yet little research has examined how these regimes enable or block attempts of public sector organizations to redesign their performance measurement (PM) systems. This study addresses that gap by developing an analytical framework built around the concept of lock-in mechanisms, which provides a structured way to identify regulatory, material, behavioral and discursive barriers to the redesign of public sector PM. This framework is then applied to the performance regime governing Danish employment services, where municipal job centers are actively trying to redesign their PM systems to better reflect client experiences and value creation. Our findings reveal that redesign efforts are constrained by lock-in mechanisms operating at three distinct levels: within the institutional context, mechanisms entrench upward accountability as the dominant purpose of PM; at the level of performance actors, mechanisms preserve rigid boundaries between those who are measured and those who do the measuring; and at the level of performance interventions, mechanisms sustain top-down uses of performance information, limiting more bottom-up approaches.

title: Revisiting the venerable debate on strategy content and public service performance
Differentiating distributed leadership: introducing distributed professional development leadership and its motivational consequences
abstract: Traditional hierarchical approaches to governing and leading public professionals have not always proven successful, and integrative and hybrid perspectives on professionalism are therefore receiving increasing attention. This study integrates professional development leadership (PDL) and distributed leadership (DL) theory and introduces the concept of distributed professional development leadership (D-PDL). D-PDL implies that employees without formal leadership responsibilities are engaged in core PDL activities focused on facilitating and realizing a shared understanding of professionalism within the scope of organizational goals. The study theorizes that professionals’ engagement in D-PDL leads to more autonomous motivation than engagement in generic DL, which covers a broad range of leadership activities that are disconnected from the professional core task. Survey data from approximately 2,400 Danish medical doctors support the theoretical framework and show that doctors’ engagement in D-PDL is associated with more intrinsic motivation and public service motivation, whereas their engagement in generic DL is primarily associated with extrinsic motivation. The study emphasizes the relevance of moving PDL beyond a leader-centric concept and of distinguishing between different types of DL activities.

title: Elites by design? How organisational structures shape assignment concentration in local government
abstract: Local government is often celebrated as democracy’s training ground, yet political authority at this level can be far more concentrated than democratic ideals suggest. This article examines how political offices accumulate among a few individuals in Swedish municipalities – a critical case given Sweden’s strong democratic norms and exceptional decentralisation. If oligarchic tendencies emerge here, they are likely to appear anywhere. Using original data from 27 strategically sampled municipalities, we map political assignments across councils, committees, and municipally owned corporations, and introduce a novel measure of ‘assignment inequality’ that captures top-heaviness in local power structures. Our findings challenge the widespread assumption that elite concentration primarily results from small scale or limited recruitment pools. Instead, institutional design – particularly corporatisation – proves decisive. Municipalities with extensive corporate networks exhibit systematically higher concentration and more skewed distributions of political authority. Local elites, we conclude, emerge by design, not default.

title: Interpretable and uncertainty-quantified early remaining useful life prediction for lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols
abstract: Under fast-charging protocols, accurately and interpretably predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries during the initial cycling stage is of great significance for early fault warning and reliability assessment. To improve the interpretability of RUL prediction, this paper proposes a causal learning approach to conduct causal analysis on domain-specific features, identifying key causal variables and systematically uncovering their relationships with RUL. To enhance the model’s capacity to fit complex nonlinear relationships and generalize across various conditions, we propose a neural network based on Legendre polynomial orthogonal bases, termed LegendreNet. Its approximation ability and theoretical validity are rigorously demonstrated. The causally selected domain features are fed into LegendreNet for prediction. In parallel, the original features are fed into a causal convolutional neural network (CCNN) to extract deep representations, capturing both global spatiotemporal dependencies and local feature details. The outputs of LegendreNet and CCNN are then concatenated and fused via LegendreNet to generate the final RUL prediction. Based on this architecture, we propose a novel multimodal prediction framework for early RUL estimation of lithium-ion batteries, named LNCCNN. Finally, to adaptively adjust the bandwidth and quantify predictive uncertainty, we introduce curvature adjustment into the Bayesian bootstrap kernel density estimation (BB-KDE) framework and propose a novel method, called curvature-aware BB-KDE (CA-BB-KDE). Experimental results on two distinct batches from the same fast-charging dataset demonstrate improved early RUL prediction accuracy, reducing RMSE by 2.96% and 7.09% and MAPE by 1.32% and 8.16%, respectively, supporting lifetime monitoring and decision-making in battery management systems.

title: From electrode scaffold to hydrogen-system value: a reverse-boundary qualification framework for direct seawater electrolysis
Semantic-aware robust PV forecasting based on a localized enhanced LLM framework
abstract: High-quality photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the operation of modern power systems. However, conventional methods rely heavily on extensive historical data, leading to a significant decline in forecasting accuracy in data-scarce scenarios such as newly built plants or extreme weather conditions. To compensate for this lack of numerical data, incorporating supplementary textual and semantic information offers a promising approach. Current PV forecasting methods have yet to fully exploit the potential of this approach. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong generalization in time-series forecasting. Furthermore, their multimodal reasoning abilities present an opportunity to bridge the inherent gap between numerical data and natural language. Motivated by these insights, we propose a localized enhanced LLM framework for robust day-ahead PV forecasting. By incorporating a semantic self-expansion mechanism and specialized embedders into a fine-tuning architecture, the framework fuses time-series data with textual information, allowing the LLM to adaptively capture forecasting-relevant features, which effectively mitigates the accuracy decline caused by data scarcity. Empirical evaluations across geographically distinct regions in China demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models like Autoformer, PatchTST, GPT4TS, and Time-LLM, highlighting the learning capabilities and robustness of our method under data scarcity.

title: Modeling multicycle anodic degradation in hard carbon-based sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Due to abundant raw materials and ecological friendliness, sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are considered a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for energy storage applications. This assertion is based on the recent advances in technology and the proven capabilities of SIBs. Physics-based modeling (PBM) is a cost-effective approach for understanding the electrochemical kinetics and degradation mechanisms of batteries. In this paper, the authors developed a single-particle model with electrolyte interactions (SPMe) coupled with anodic degradation in a sodium vanadium phosphate fluoride (NVPF)/Hard carbon cell. Stress generation due to intercalation, adsorption, and pore-filling is considered. Degradation due to sodium plating/stripping with dead sodium storage, solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth/fracture, and loss of active material is simulated at a 1C charging rate over 300 cycles. The developed model is shown to be reliable for predicting capacity degradation and discharge profiles. The model provides insight into the suppression of SEI and dead sodium, and their effects on resistance during battery aging. The results show the role of initial SEI thickness variation (1 nm–20 nm) across different levels of dead sodium storage (1%–5%). Ultimately, the capacity degradation is assessed for the simulated cell. The proposed model can serve as a reference for the design of SIBs.

title: Loss visibility versus spatial detail in industrial district-heating dispatch optimisation
Machine learning-accelerated discovery and optimization of thermoelectric materials for energy conversion
abstract: Recently, machine learning (ML) has received growing attention as a powerful tool for accelerating the discovery and optimization of thermoelectric materials. By utilizing large-scale datasets generated from high-throughput calculations and experimental measurements, ML models are able to efficiently predict key properties, identify promising candidates, and guide material design. Herein we summarize the latest progress in this rapidly evolving field and present a comprehensive overview on typical ML workflows, key algorithms and efficient models for predicting thermoelectric properties, including both indirect and direct predictions of electrical and thermal transport characteristics. Subsequently, we discuss how ML facilitates the discovery of novel thermoelectric materials and supports the optimization of composition, synthesis processes, and microstructures. Finally, we explore current challenges and future opportunities for integrating ML into thermoelectric investigation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of ML applications in thermoelectrics, thereby highlighting their potential to accelerate thermoelectric materials development for energy conversion and waste-heat recovery applications.

title: Bridging the environmental and economic gaps: operation reality and sustainability of real-world green hydrogen plants
Advances in microwave-assisted catalytic and plasma conversion of methane: A comprehensive review
abstract: Microwave-assisted methane (CH 4 ) conversion offers a transformative pathway for hydrogen and syngas production. This review systematically examines microwave catalysis and microwave plasma technologies across four key routes: methane pyrolysis (MP), dry reforming (DRM), steam reforming (SMR), and partial oxidation (POM). Microwave irradiation reduces activation energy by up to 45% for MP (from 45.5 to 24.8 kJ/mol) and 29% for DRM (from 90.8 to 64.2 kJ/mol for CH 4 ), while enabling 250 °C lower operating temperatures compared to conventional heating. Microwave plasma achieves CH 4 conversion >90% at near-ambient bulk temperatures, and variable-frequency microwave enables in-situ catalyst reactivation for stable operation >1300 min. Despite these advantages, most microwave-assisted systems remain at TRL 3–7, with key challenges including non-uniform heating, catalyst deactivation, and scale-up. By critically comparing thermal vs. non-thermal effects and microwave catalysis vs. plasma, this review identifies research priorities: microwave-specific catalyst design, reactor engineering for uniform field distribution, and integration with renewable electricity. This work provides a quantitative foundation for advancing microwave-assisted methane conversion from laboratory discovery toward industrial deployment.

title: Adaptive multi-timescale coordinated control of hybrid energy storage with RoCoF-driven dynamic allocation for frequency security and lifecycle optimization in low-inertia power systems
abstract: The global energy transition has led to a continuous decline in power system inertia, driven by high renewable penetration, large-scale electrification, and frequent extreme events, thereby exacerbating frequency stability risks. Conventional frequency or inertia support approaches are insufficient to simultaneously satisfy the requirements of rapid response, sustained support, and economic efficiency in low-inertia systems. Hybrid energy storage systems leverage the complementary advantages of power-type and energy-type resources, enabling coordinated support across multiple timescales from inertia response to energy dispatch. As a representative power-type resource, flywheel energy storage emulates the rotational inertia of synchronous generators and exhibits high power density, fast response, and long cycle life, making it suited for mitigating high-frequency disturbances. However, the high unit energy cost of flywheel energy storage limits its capacity, leading to energy depletion under sustained disturbances and forcing batteries to absorb high-frequency fluctuations, thereby accelerating degradation. To address the limitations of conventional static allocation rules and the lack of explicit coupling with real-time nonlinear frequency dynamics in low-inertia grids, this study proposes a multi-task adaptive coordinated control strategy for hybrid energy storage under high renewable penetration. A dynamic weighting mechanism, which mathematically maps the rigorous physical safety boundaries onto a Sigmoid adaptive perception coefficient driven by the rate of change of frequency, is developed to enable frequency-band separation and demand-oriented task allocation. To execute this mechanism, a three-layer coordinated architecture is designed. Specifically, the perception layer quantifies disturbance severity, the coordination layer dynamically reconfigures task weights to resolve resource conflicts, and the execution layer performs physical power mapping. In addition, a variable-gain scheduling factor is introduced to mitigate capacity depletion, and a multi-timescale optimization model considering battery degradation is developed to improve the lifecycle economic performance. The results indicate that the proposed strategy improves frequency stability, reduces battery degradation, and enhances economic performance.

title: Data-enhanced economic model predictive control for sustainable wastewater treatment: energy optimization and GHG mitigation in cold regions
abstract: For future low-carbon wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), comprehensive performances including effluent quality, energy costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions need to be optimized urgently. The WWTPs in cold regions face unique challenges characterized by low water temperatures, significant seasonal fluctuations, and high energy costs. Traditional control methods struggle to address these issues due to a lack of predictive capabilities. Accordingly, we proposed a novel data-enhanced economic model predictive control (DEMPC) strategy. This approach innovatively developed temperature-adapted deep neural network (DNN) models by enhanced datasets, thereby providing a fast and accurate prediction model for control strategy. Furthermore, multi-step prediction and rolling optimization were implemented based on EMPC to simultaneously optimize multiple operational variables under seasonal temperature fluctuations. A validation study was conducted at a municipal WWTP in the cold climate of Northeast China, comparing two energy recovery scenarios (with and without combined heat and power, CHP). The results show that energy optimization and GHG emissions reduction were achieved in both cases. Under the CHP scenario, the DEMPC strategy achieved reductions of 25.73% in energy costs and 24.92% in GHG emissions compared to the original control strategy. The proposed control framework possesses prediction-driven temperature adaptability and significant advantages in energy saving and carbon reduction, providing a new technical pathway for the sustainable operation of cold-region WWTPs.

title: Predicting Future Land Use and Land Cover Dynamics in a Tropical Watershed for Irrigation Planning and Agricultural Sustainability Using a Hybrid Modelling Approach
Priorities and potential for enlarging Czech large-scale protected areas
Plant-derived green nanomaterials: From biosynthesis to biocompatible applications in sustainable agriculture
abstract: Traditional nanotechnology, relying on chemical reagents, generating ecological residues, and showing limited compatibility with plant physiology, faces challenges in meeting the requirements of green and sustainable agriculture. Plant-derived green nanomaterials have therefore emerged as an environmentally friendly alternative. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in their synthesis, focusing on three strategies: plant extract-mediated reduction, agricultural waste-templated synthesis, and plant metabolism-guided in situ synthesis. The differences in plant species, tissues, and metabolic components can influence the formation and regulation of nanomaterials, while plant-derived components participate in reduction, nucleation, growth, and stabilization, contributing to the formation of plant-derived interfacial structures. A multidimensional characterization framework tailored to plant systems is proposed, integrating indicators and methodologies for structural evaluation and biosafety assessment. The mechanisms underlying their roles in seed germination regulation, precise nutrient delivery, and the enhancement of plant stress resistance are systematically categorized and discussed. The ecological implications of their environmental transformation, persistence, and biocompatibility are discussed. Future directions focus on artificial intelligence, value‑added agricultural waste utilization, and full life‑cycle performance evaluation. Overall, this review provides theoretical and practical guidance for advancing plant‑derived green nanotechnology toward sustainable agriculture, food security, and ecological security.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of critical materials demand and embodied carbon emissions of electric vehicle batteries across Chinese provinces
Life cycle assessment of electrochemical direct ocean capture: scope 1–3 carbon accounting and supply chain hotspots
Quantifying Spatially Dynamic Transportation Carbon Footprint of New Energy Batteries: The GIS-LCA Based Interpretable Approach
abstract: Abstract This study focuses on the transportation-driven spatial characteristics and dynamics, carbon footprint (CF), and environmental impact of new energy batteries from material acquisition to manufacturing. Based on the life cycle assessment (LCA) method, transportation data are obtained through the GIS-LCA platform to construct a quantification framework for analyzing the railway transportation CF of lithium-ion, solid-state (Li-FeS2, LLZO, LiPON), and hydrogen fuel cells (HFCs). Within a cradle-to-grave life cycle framework, transportation CF varies across battery technologies. NMC batteries show comparatively higher transport-related CF (0.512 kgCO2 eq), while HFC systems show lower values (0.00973 kgCO2 eq), primarily driven by raw material type, transportation distance, and the spatial distribution of production bases. The transportation CF accounts for less than 10% of the production phase, but its path spatial dynamics and regional logistics network differences lead to significant carbon emission (CE) distribution variations, such as PVC transportation CEs in the Shanghai base being over 95% lower than those in Beijing. The study provides scientific support for low-carbon technology pathway selection, supply chain layout optimization, and regional collaborative emission reduction in the battery industry. These findings support localized sourcing and spatially optimized supply chains to reduce the level of transportation emissions.

title: Controlled Ion Dehydration-Driven Catalysis Enabled by Reverse-Mode Nanofiltration
abstract: Abstract Catalysis under nanoscale confinement is widely pursued, but practical systems remain limited by a persistent contradiction: maximizing confinement-enhanced reactivity usually increases the residence time and accelerates pore failure. Here we present a ceramic nanofiltration platform that resolves this trade-off by coupling subnanometer confinement with transient, flow-through ion dehydration. The membrane is constructed by atomic layer deposition on a hierarchical α-Al2O3/γ-Al2O3 scaffold, yielding a robust, ultrathin Al2O3 active layer with tunable nanochannels and minimized transport distance to the reaction interface. During transmembrane permeation, Fe2+ ions are partially dehydrated, exposing vacant coordination sites that immediately react with H2O2 upon emergence to degrade organic micropollutants (e.g., tetracycline). This synergistic process yields a kinetic enhancement ratio of 90.5% for the dehydration group relative to the corresponding rehydration group. The kinetic enhancement ratio obtained with the commercial polyamide nanofiltration membrane NF270 under the same comparison framework was substantially lower. Beyond activity, the inorganic architecture sustains 30 d of continuous backwashing with <3% fluctuation in pure-water permeability and exhibits a kinetic enhancement ratio of 89.6% after backwashing. Importantly, the reverse-mode configuration reduces reliance on prolonged reactant residence within nanopores, thereby lowering the risk of pore blockage. These results establish a membrane-enabled strategy for capturing nonequilibrium ionic states and thereby translate nanoconfinement chemistry into an operationally durable format, with broad implications for water treatment, electrochemical conversion, and selective resource recovery.

title: MiRA: A Multi-Receptive Integration Framework for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Pathways in AOPs─A Case Study of UV and Far-UV Systems
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of pollutant transformation pathways in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) is critical for precise treatment design. However, conventional models inadequately capture global dependencies and key local reaction information, limiting reliable inference of complex multistep pathways. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces the multireceptive integration for reaction-pathway analysis (MiRA) framework. For the first time, it integrates “multi-receptive field chemical semantic capture + learnable fusion decision-making” into AOPdegradation pathway prediction. This enables the collaborative expression of local reaction sites, neighborhood structures, and global conditional dependencies within a single model, yielding information-rich feature representations with superior generalization capabilities. Using ultraviolet (UV) and far-ultraviolet (far-UV) data sets, MiRA framework achieves accuracies of 88.03% and 85.44%, respectively, with BLEU scores of 0.9459 and 0.9325, and Tanimoto similarity scores of 0.9405 and 0.9296, demonstrating robust predictive precision. Attention visualizations reveal that the framework automatically identifies key reaction features of substrates, demonstrating a degree of expert-level chemical reasoning capability. Additionally, an integrated toxicity estimation module provides relative screening of the toxicity potentials of transformation products. Overall, this study provides an intelligent analytical method for predicting pollutant transformation pathways and screening the toxicity potentials of transformation products in AOPs. It offers new methodological support for the precise design of AOPs.

title: Metal–Organic Frameworks with Tunable Metal Node for Selective Capture and Separation of CO2 and CO from Ternary Blast Furnace Gas Mixtures
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous capture of carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO) from complex industrial gases represents a critical challenge. Designing framework sorbents that combine selective molecular recognition with stability is essential. Herein, a series of anthracene-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), M-ABHBs (M = Co, Mg, Mn, and Ni), were successfully synthesized. By regulating metal centers, which leads to different interactions between gases (CO2/CO/N2) and metal–ligand pairs in the framework, excellent CO adsorption selectivity has been discovered. Notably, Mg/Mn-ABHBs allow efficient binary CO2/N2 separation, and Co/Ni-ABHBs enable benchmark ternary CO2/CO/N2 separation by increasing the adsorption affinity toward CO. This unique phenomenon is rare among adsorbents. Such behaviors enable a stepwise separation strategy to selectively capture CO2 and CO from ternary mixtures. Co-ABHB exhibits high selectivity of CO/N2 (13.1), while Mg-ABHB shows high selectivity of CO2/N2 (66.6) and CO2/CO (5.8). In situ DRIFTS and theoretical calculations indicate that the former is the result of the strong interactions of Co-CO in the cavities of Co-ABHB, while Mg sites strongly capture only CO2, not CO. Breakthrough tests show that from a CO2/CO/N2 mixture, M-ABHBs demonstrated excellent separation performance. This work offers a design strategy for efficient carbon capture under complex industrial gas conditions.

title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
A two-condenser DHW heat pump for flexible heating: Assessing carbon savings using hourly grid emissions
abstract: Current building decarbonization policies often prioritize on-site renewable energy generation, an approach that is frequently unfeasible for block residential buildings with limited space for photovoltaic (PV) installations, as it is the case of many buildings in Spain. As national electricity grids become increasingly renewable, utilizing hourly grid CO 2 emission profiles rather than annual average provides more realistic results. In 2024, annual average CO 2 emissions in the Spanish grid was 0.096 kg CO 2 /kWh, while hourly CO 2 emission factors calculated month by month ranged from 0.047 kg CO 2 /kWh to 0.180 kg CO 2 /kWh. This article presents an innovative heat pump with two condensers that improves its COP and controls usage times in order to reduce CO 2 emissions associated with consumption. This new design is a solution that allows to pursue the flexibility of the systems, one of the key points of European regulations. Then the performance of the unit with two condensers is compared to a conventional one-condenser unit, results show that while standard annual-average assessments estimate a CO 2 emission reduction of up to 18%, applying an hourly evaluation reveals CO 2 emission savings exceeding 35%. This work highlights the problems with the current evaluation of heat pumps and the need to evaluate their associated CO 2 emissions more accurately, either through the use of electricity obtained from the grid or even by the use of on-site photovoltaic panels.

title: Enhancing rapid removal of iron from recycled aluminium based on reducing interfacial mass transfer resistance by an immersion rotational segregation process
abstract: Recycling of aluminum scrap is a crucial pathway for carbon reduction in the aluminum industry, as its carbon emissions represent only 3%-5% of those from primary aluminum production. However, a great challenge is to further remove trace iron content to a certain range in order to meet the requirements of multi grade high-end aluminum alloys. Herein, a novel immersion rotational segregation process (IRSP) is proposed to remove trace iron content in short time, which effectively reduces interfacial mass transfer resistance due to boundary layer thinning. Kilogram-scale experiments show that a single-stage process achieves a 60% iron removal efficiency within 3 min. By employing a two-stage treatment, the Fe content is successfully reduced from 0.8 wt% to below 0.15 wt%, meeting the stringent purity standards for high-quality aluminum alloy raw materials. This rapid purification is driven by intense shear forces that induce complex fluid interactions within high-speed shear zone and vortex zones, compressing the concentration boundary layer to 0.31 mm and significantly reducing interfacial mass transfer resistance. Furthermore, 100-kg scale-up experiments were performed to validate the industrial viability of the process, achieving an iron removal efficiency exceeding 70% within 20 min. This method provides a efficient pathway for the high-value upcycling of aluminium scrap, significantly reducing reliance on primary aluminum consumption and contributing to substantial carbon emission reductions in the global aluminum industry.

title: Explainable Machine Learning Reveals Spatially Heterogeneous BOD–COD Relationships in a Large River Basin to Inform Targeted Monitoring Strategies
Mitigating thermal degradation of cement paste at elevated temperatures via ultra-fine magnesite tailings incorporation
Use of incineration bottom ash for geopolymer electrolytes in structural supercapacitors
Data-driven predictive control for combined-cycle gas turbines by multi-agent reinforcement learning
abstract: Fast and reliable load following is increasingly required as variable wind and photovoltaic generation expand. Combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs) are widely adopted to provide this flexibility. In a “2+1” CCGT, two gas turbines (GTs) are directly actuated, whereas the shared steam turbine (ST) contributes delayed power through heat-recovery and steam-cycle dynamics. A hierarchical framework combining improved model-free adaptive predictive control (IMFAPC), an extended state observer (ESO), and multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO), termed MAPPO-IMFAPC-ESO, is developed. A data-driven digital twin is formed from dynamic GT surrogates and a history-dependent ST model. Deterministic nominal commands are generated by ESO-enhanced IMFAPC (ESO-IMFAPC). Scaled and bounded residual corrections are allocated by MAPPO from local GT observations and the shared gross-generation error. Under a uniform contraction condition and bounded aggregate remainders, a conditional uniform ultimate boundedness estimate is derived for the exact-solve baseline. The fixed-policy implementation is characterized by conditional input-to-state practical stability under bounded deployment perturbations. Chronological leave-one-dataset-out validation confirms high one-step predictive accuracy of the ST model, with an RMSE of 1.920 MW and R 2 = 0.9874 , while held-out recursive command-replay tests reveal appreciable long-horizon error accumulation in the coupled GT–ST surrogate. Accordingly, the closed-loop results are interpreted as relative controller comparisons within a common learned digital-twin environment. Across five independently trained MAPPO-IMFAPC-ESO policies, the staircase gross-generation RMSE is 0.919 ± 0.014 MW, demonstrating repeatable sub-MW tracking, and a separate 24-hour evaluation shows no progressive growth of tracking error. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed hierarchical framework provides a unified data-driven approach for coordinating fast GT actuation with delayed ST response, while preserving deterministic predictive regulation and introducing bounded multi-agent residual coordination for CCGT load following.

title: Capital value of shared wind-to-hydrogen infrastructure in co-located green ammonia and liquefied hydrogen plants
abstract: Co-locating green liquefied hydrogen (LH 2 ) and ammonia (NH 3 ) production creates a shared-infrastructure capital-allocation problem. This study develops a multi-year mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework to evaluate how an imposed LH 2 requirement changes the design, service, and installed-capital requirements of an off-grid wind-powered NH 3 platform. The model uses chronological ERA5 wind data from Chile’s Magallanes region and represents shared wind generation, desalination, electrolysis, and hydrogen buffering together with the dedicated NH 3 and LH 2 conversion and storage pathways. Four planning scenarios are compared: an NH 3 -only benchmark, fixed-budget co-production, protected-NH 3 co-production through marginal capacity expansion, and standalone greenfield LH 2 production. The analysis distinguishes the service tradeoff created when LH 2 is introduced under a fixed capital budget from the additional investment required when benchmark NH 3 service is protected. The results show that co-location reduces the incremental capital required to provide LH 2 relative to a standalone greenfield system, but this advantage does not arise uniformly from all shared assets. Instead, the integrated design combines expansion of the common wind-to-hydrogen platform with lower requirements for parts of the dedicated LH 2 pathway, particularly liquefaction capacity. The principal capital-value conclusions remain robust to constrained downstream process flexibility, stronger NH 3 service protection, hourly temporal resolution, spatial wind-resource variation, wind-plant losses, turbine representation, LH 2 service scale, and major CAPEX assumptions. The findings provide plant-gate, CAPEX-centered planning insights into when co-location can reduce the incremental infrastructure required to introduce LH 2 production while maintaining renewable NH 3 service.

title: Linking micropollutant gradients and multigenerational microplastic exposure to insecticide tolerance in field populations of Anopheles gambiae s.l
abstract: Urban freshwater systems increasingly serve as breeding habitats for Anopheles gambiae ; however , the effects of prolonged larval exposure to complex waterborne pollutants remain insufficiently characterised. Therefore, larvae were collected from two mosquito breeding sites with pronounced spatial differences in baseline concentrations of heavy metals (Pb, Cd, Hg, As), pesticides (organochlorines/organophosphates), inorganic nutrients (NO₃ − , NO₂ − , NH₄ + , PO₄ 3− ), and microplastics (MPs). Principal Component Analysis demonstrated a pronounced difference in the overall pollutant profiles of the two breeding sites, with substantially greater contamination at the downstream site. The influence of repeated exposure to MPs and the insecticide deltamethrin (either on its own or with MPs) on field populations of larvae was quantified in laboratory experiments. Larval survival and development were recorded over six generations, and insecticide tolerance of adult mosquitoes derived from these larvae quantified by WHO resistance bioassay tests. Initially, MP exposure reduced larval survival and delayed development; however, after several generations, larvae exhibited increased survival, accelerated development, and enhanced adult tolerance to deltamethrin. These responses were more pronounced in mosquitoes originating from the more polluted site, suggesting potential pre-existing environmental conditioning, although differences in sibling-species composition between sites cannot be excluded as a contributing factor. Exposure to combined MPs and insecticide resulted in higher survival and shorter development times compared to insecticide exposure alone. Collectively, these findings provide evidence that repeated MP exposure, in conjunction with environmental pollution, can progressively increase phenotypic insecticide tolerance in An. gambiae . Polluted urban breeding habitats may therefore contribute to reduced insecticide susceptibility, emphasizing the need to incorporate environmental pollution considerations into vector-control and insecticide-susceptibility management strategies.

title: Assessment of the technical feasibility of pruning waste gasification in a pilot-scale downdraft plant
How Low-Level Jets Impact the Power Curve of Floating Offshore Wind Turbines: Comprehensive Analysis and Prediction Model
abstract: The wind turbine power curve, essential for wind turbine monitoring, is typically modeled assuming uniform or shear inflow. However, the low-level jet disrupts this conventional single-point wind speed to power relationship due to its unique wind profile, causing significant actual power output deviations. To enhance power curve prediction under low-level jet conditions, this study introduces a low-level jet model from measurements. The research methodology progresses by first quantifying the sensitivity of power output to low-level jet characteristics, followed by an analysis of how low-level jets impact the power curve, ultimately leading to a new minute-level model. The findings identify three low-level jet characteristics (jet height, jet intensity, and friction velocity) that significantly impact the power curve, causing deviations up to 32.91% from the reference. Moreover, friction velocity significantly affects power fluctuations, impairing the accuracy of real-time minute-level power prediction and control. By acquiring these characteristics through wind field perception technology and integrating the proposed model, which considers only the jet height and jet intensity, minute-level power prediction errors can be effectively reduced. Furthermore, based on the actual power curve, the control strategy's switching criterion can be adjusted to the actual rated wind speed. This reduces energy losses from existing strategies.

title: Balancing Profit and Exergy Efficiency: Optimal Dispatch Strategies for Integrated Energy Systems with High Renewable Penetration
Estimating daily run-of-river hydropower generation from open hydrometeorological data: Limits of hydrology-based modelling
abstract: Hydropower is important for energy system modelling, where run-of-river hydropower is commonly represented as prescribed non-dispatchable generation. This study uses open hydrometeorological datasets to estimate the aggregated daily run-of-river generation and to assess the explanatory limits of hydrology-based modelling. ERA5, GEOGLOWS V2, and GloFAS v4.0 reanalyses are evaluated against reported generation for six European countries as a case study: France, Austria, Germany, Finland, Portugal, and Romania. Different input sets are compared within a consistent modelling framework, and the best-performing baseline model is used to diagnose remaining estimation errors. The results show that GloFAS river discharge provides the most suitable input for reproducing reported run-of-river generation, as it captures the dominant seasonal hydrological variability more robustly than the models with ERA5 and GEOGLOWS. The remaining error is the uncaptured short-term variation in reported generation. Additional tests indicate that accounting for reservoir generation provides limited improvements in model performance at the aggregated daily country level, while part of the residual is associated with electricity-price deviations, potentially reflecting short-term operation enabled by unclassified pondage within reported run-of-river generation. Accordingly, representing reported run-of-river generation as fully non-dispatchable in large-scale energy system models may overlook the potential short-term flexibility contained in the reported profiles The hydrology-based run-of-river estimates should therefore be interpreted as weather-dependent availability profiles, and the reproducible workflow in this study can produce such profiles for large-scale energy system studies across historical weather years beyond the period covered by reported data.

title: Thermal Serial-Parallel Combined Coupling in a PV-TEG-PCM System to Mitigate the PV-Cooling/TEG-Output Trade-Off and Enhance Full-Day Efficiency
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer efficiency losses and unstable output at high operating temperatures and under shading or nighttime conditions. Integrating thermoelectric generators (TEGs) and phase change materials (PCMs) can improve heat recovery and thermal regulation, but conventional stacked PV–TEG–PCM systems face a trade-off between reducing PV temperature to improve PV output and maintaining the TEG temperature difference to enhance thermoelectric output. To address this issue, this study proposes a PV–TEG–PCM hybrid system based on thermal serial–parallel combined coupling (TSPC). The PCM and TEG are co-located on the PV rear side, and a copper heat-spreading path enables direct PV–PCM heat transfer while retaining thermoelectric heat recovery. Simulations and experiments compare standalone PV, PV–TEG, conventional PV–TEG–PCM, and TSPC configurations under steady, fluctuating, full-day, and outdoor conditions. Compared with the conventional PV–TEG–PCM system, TSPC reduces PV temperature fluctuation by 56.67% under fluctuating irradiance. Under full-day operation, it lowers the daytime mean PV temperature by 14 °C and increases the mean daytime PV power by 8.02%. The 24 h total energy output is increased by 7.76%, with a 24 h mean power of 435.92 mW. Outdoor testing in Shenzhen further verifies the feasibility of TSPC, with a measured peak PV temperature of 46.43 °C under cloudy conditions. Overall, TSPC provides an effective coupling strategy for improving PV thermal regulation and full-day energy utilization.

title: Experimental study on the estimation of venting efficiency and the risk of low-temperature damage to pipe walls during the manual venting process of large-scale dense phase CO2 pipelines
A simulation-guided roadmap to efficient ethanol production via carbon monoxide electrolysis
abstract: Electrochemical ethanol production via carbon monoxide reduction reaction (CORR) offers a promising alternative to conventional routes, but practical implementation requires improvements in selectivity, current density, and single-pass conversion efficiency (SPCE). Here, we couple insights from multi-physics modeling and techno-economic analysis for CORR-to-ethanol in scalable membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzers, with the aim of identifying pathways to match today’s ethanol price. The model resolves the local reaction environment, voltage-loss distribution, and system performance under various operating, structural, transport, and kinetic parameters. A one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analysis is performed to identify the parameters that strongly affect the ethanol partial current density, followed by Taguchi optimization to determine favorable parameter combinations. Scenario analysis reveals that kinetics-related parameters primarily govern ethanol selectivity while kinetic and system improvements contribute to current density and SPCE. The ideal-performance case electrolyzer configuration and operation conditions enable a full-cell ethanol energy efficiency (EE) of 57.3% (1.83 V) and an ethanol SPCE of 89.1% at a current density of 704 mA cm -2 . This performance corresponds to an ethanol electroproduction cost of 1,594 $ ton -1 , approximately 47% lower than literature benchmarks.

title: wind energy harvesting from flow-induced vibrations of cylinder with separated wake plate
Designing an Optimal Biogas Plant Network for Food Waste: Impacts of Recycling Targets on Waste-to-Energy Systems

An Integrated Assessment Framework for Salt Cavern Energy Storage Pathways in China under Site Constraints and Technology Maturity
Two-stage robust planning of a rural electricity–heat–gas–biomass system with cluster-specific uncertainty sets and a worst-case-day budget
Syngas Production from Sewage Sludge–Waste Oil Co-Gasification: Thermodynamic and Exergy Analysis
abstract: Sewage sludge is a low-grade feedstock for thermochemical conversion due to its high ash content, low volatile fraction, and low energy density, which restrict syngas quality and thermodynamic efficiency. In contrast, hydrocarbon-rich waste oils provide high chemical energy and reactivity but exhibit instability when processed independently. This study introduces a co-gasification strategy that integrates sewage sludge with waste oils to shift the governing reaction regime from heterogeneous char conversion toward gas-phase reforming, thereby intensifying hydrogen generation and improving thermodynamic performance. Experiments were conducted under varying oxidant types, flow rates, and temperatures to elucidate process behavior. The results demonstrate that co-gasification enhances hydrogen-rich syngas production and improves energy and exergy performance. Under oxygen-blown conditions, hydrogen concentration increased from approximately 42 to 54 vol%, accompanied by increases in CH 4 and CO fractions and an improvement in syngas calorific value. Optimal hydrogen-rich syngas production was achieved at 700 °C and low oxidant flow rates (0.01–0.05 L min −1 ), where reducing conditions favored reforming-dominated pathways and elevated H 2 /CO ratios. Thermodynamic evaluation revealed that the sludge–motor oil system increased first-law efficiency from 0.264 to 0.394 and exergy efficiency from 0.217 to 0.337. Feedstock-specific exergy analysis further indicated that the thermodynamic response of the system was governed by the distribution and recovery of chemical exergy rather than feed mass alone. Furthermore, a multiple linear regression model (R 2 = 0.991) described the empirical relationship between syngas composition and calorific value under the investigated operating conditions. Overall, the proposed co-gasification strategy offers a robust pathway for the thermodynamic upgrading of low-grade wastes into hydrogen-rich syngas for advanced energy systems.

title: Nanoporous Molecular Springs as Energy-Density Extenders for Liquid-Piston Compressed Air Energy Storage: A Performance and Techno-Economic Assessment
Does low-carbon policy improve the environmental performance in China?
abstract: This study examines the impacts and driving mechanisms of low-carbon policy on environmental performance, with a focus on both direct policy effects and the underlying structural drivers. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions and years, the analysis employs a combination of econometric modeling and configurational approaches to capture heterogeneous and non-linear relationships. The results indicate that low-carbon policy significantly improves environmental performance, particularly in terms of emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and pollution control. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary across regions depending on differences in economic development, industrial structure, and governance capacity. Further analysis reveals that technological innovation, green investment, regulatory intensity, and public participation are key driving factors that jointly shape policy effectiveness. The study also identifies multiple pathways through which these factors interact to enhance environmental outcomes, highlighting the importance of synergistic policy design. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how low-carbon goals translate into measurable environmental improvements and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to optimize policy implementation in diverse socio-economic contexts.

title: Spatial associations with estimated net migration in Osaka, 2015–2020: A grid-level machine learning approach
abstract: As Japan faces rapid depopulation, distinguishing net migration from natural population changes is important for understanding local population dynamics at fine spatial scales. This study proposes a data-driven framework to identify factors associated with census-derived estimates of net migration in Osaka Prefecture at a high-resolution 500 m grid level over the period 2015–2020. Methodologically, we first refined the census survival-ratio method by introducing calibration parameters fitted to prefecture-level Basic Resident Register migration totals, thereby improving age-specific aggregate alignment. Subsequently, spatial associations were analyzed using a machine learning pipeline based on LightGBM. To address the multicollinearity inherent in spatial socioeconomic data—a persistent challenge in urban modeling—we integrated variable clustering with Owen values, a game-theoretic attribution method. This approach allowed us to estimate model-attributed contributions while accounting for groups of highly correlated variables. The analysis revealed “mosaic-like” dynamics characterized by sharp intra-regional contrasts. Specifically, we identified spatial patterns among younger populations that were consistent with the “return to the city” phenomenon during the study period and strongly associated with high-rise condominiums, contrasting with estimated net outflows from aging suburban public housing districts. These findings demonstrate that this high-resolution, explainable AI approach can capture complex, non-uniform spatial patterns of estimated net migration and provide an exploratory basis for identifying area characteristics that warrant further investigation.
journal_name: Environment and Planning B: Urban Analytics and City Science

title: Roads and carbon: Suburbanisation versus induced demand in U.S. states
A Review of Building Climate‐Resilient Agriculture in Smallholder Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change has increasingly threatened agricultural sustainability and food security, especially in smallholder farming systems where limited resources and adaptive capacity constrain responses to climate shocks. This study systematically reviews the literature on agricultural climate resilience, focusing on resilience measurement, farmer adaptation, organizational support, and government regulation. The review shows that resilience research has evolved from vulnerability‐oriented approaches toward broader frameworks emphasizing resistance, recovery, adaptation, and transformation capacities. Existing studies indicate that farmers’ adaptive behaviors, such as production adjustment and technology adoption, form the micro‐level foundation of resilience. However, smallholders often face constraints in information, capital, technology, and market access, limiting the effectiveness of autonomous adaptation. Organizational support and government regulation therefore play essential roles through information diffusion, resource coordination, infrastructure provision, policy incentives, and collective governance. Nevertheless, current research still lacks theoretical integration, dynamic resilience assessment, cross‐scale governance analysis, and systematic understanding of institutional constraints in smallholder systems. The review highlights that agricultural climate resilience is not solely determined by farmers’ adoption of adaptation technologies, but also by how resource constraints, market barriers, and institutional arrangements shape adaptation decisions and coordination among multiple actors.

title: Economics of Wind Energy: Markets, Policy, and Investment Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Wind energy is central to energy transitions, but research on its economics remains fragmented across markets, policy, finance, lifecycle costs, and system integration. This review consolidates the field by applying co‐word analysis, Louvain clustering, and tech‐mining emergence metrics to 2448 publications from 2015 to 2025. The analysis identifies ten thematic clusters covering grid integration, market design, techno‐economic assessment, policy instruments, socio‐environmental impacts, resource optimization, turbine and hybrid technologies, offshore costs, lifecycle and circular economy, and storage‐based sector coupling. The findings show increasing convergence on hybrid systems, uncertainty‐aware modeling, circularity, adaptive regulation, and investment risk management. Persistent gaps remain in quantifying externalities, evaluating lifecycle liabilities, managing revenue volatility, and designing policies that respond to technological and market change. The review offers an integrative economic framework that links energy systems, finance, and policy and provides guidance for policymakers, investors, and researchers seeking to support resilient, competitive, and inclusive wind energy deployment.

title: Banking on Culture: Individualism and Foreign Bank Ownership
journal_name: Journal of International Financial Markets Institutions & Money

title: Is the Gene‐ie Out of the Bottle? The Problems and Perils of Genetics Research in Management
abstract: Abstract In recent years, the field of management research has witnessed the emergence of a stream of research that seeks to identify the genetic determinants of managerial, entrepreneurial, and organizational behaviour. We challenge the reductionist epistemology underpinning this genetic perspective in management research and highlight the inherently weak inferences about human behaviour that follow from its prevailing methods and explanatory models. We further examine the ethical implications that arise from its underlying assumptions and potential future applications. We then propose recasting the role of genetics as part of a broader phenomenon‐driven approach towards studying and explaining human behaviour in management research and outline a conceptual framework aimed at generating stronger and contextually grounded explanatory models of managerial, entrepreneurial, and organizational behaviour.

title: The “She‐Power” in Sustainability: Female Executives, Green Human Capital Investment, and Corporate Green Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT Based on data from Chinese A‐share listed companies from 2016 to 2024, we study the impact of female executives on green human capital investment. We find that female executives are positively associated with green human capital investment. Moderating effect analyses show that this positive effect is stronger for green positions requiring higher skills, under weaker environmental regulation, and in less polluting industries. Heterogeneity analyses show that green human capital investment is more directly influenced by senior management than by the board and that the main effect is stronger in firms with high labor intensity. Further analysis reveals that green human capital investment is positively associated with subsequent green innovation. Moreover, our research confirms a critical mass effect of female executives on green human capital investment. Overall, this study reveals how female executives shape firms' investment in green human capital.

title: Green Loans: From Effects to Advantages
abstract: ABSTRACT By conducting a systematic literature review, this study examines the opportunities and threats and thus the economic implications of green loans from banks perspective. The results show a variety of heterogeneous effects of granting green loans (GL) in several areas, as market valuation, lending process, risk or profit. From a purely numerical perspective, we find more opportunities than threats, suggesting banks should provide GL. In this context, reductions in risks and nonperforming loans as well as increases in competitiveness and profits, which are contrasted in particular by increased costs, are specifically notable. However, as theoretical opportunities do not necessarily transform into real benefits, we subsequently use the dynamic capabilities framework to elaborate approaches that will enable banks to achieve long‐term competitive advantages through GL.

title: Interpreting sustainability signals: how brand origin and consumer cosmopolitanism shape CSR inferences and downstream consumer responses
abstract: Purpose As restaurants worldwide increasingly adopt plant-based offerings to advance sustainability goals, understanding how consumers interpret these initiatives has become essential. Drawing from signaling theory and social identity theory, this research aims to demonstrate that plant-based menu promotions function as corporate social responsibility (CSR) signals, with consumers’ interpretations shaped jointly by restaurant brand origin and their level of cosmopolitanism. Design/methodology/approach The research used two online experiments to test the proposed framework across different cuisine types and dining contexts. Findings Consumers low in cosmopolitanism ascribe stronger CSR to domestic (vs foreign) restaurant brands, whereas those high in cosmopolitanism show the opposite pattern. Moreover, these CSR inferences translate into enhanced product-related responses and brand-related outcomes. Originality/value This research contributes to the hospitality literature on brand origin effects, restaurant sustainable practices and CSR communication. It offers insights for hospitality firms seeking to leverage plant-based initiatives to foster positive brand inferences and enhance consumer outcomes.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: The double-edged sword effect of AI-employee collaboration on hotel employees’ digital performance: a job crafting perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the differential effects of artificial intelligence (AI)-employee collaboration on hotel employees’ digital innovation performance (DIP) and digital task performance (DTP) through job crafting, with leadership empathy (LEMP) as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach This study was conducted using multitemporal survey data from 411 hotel employees and their leaders in China. Findings The results indicate that AI-employee collaboration positively affects promotion-focused job crafting (POJC) and prevention-focused job crafting (PEJC). POJC positively affects DIP and DTP, whereas PEJC positively affects DTP but negatively affects DIP. LEMP positively moderates the link with POJC and negatively with PEJC. Practical implications This study deepens understanding of AI-employee dynamics and offers insights for improving digital performance and innovation in the digital era. Originality/value Based on regulatory focus theory, this study distinguishes employee digital performance, unveils the dual pathways of AI-employee collaboration’s influence from a job crafting perspective and expands boundary conditions by incorporating LEMP, offering theoretical insights for effective hotel AI-employee collaboration.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: From inspiration to depletion: the curvilinear effect of spiritual leadership on employee role-based performance
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the too-much-of-a-good-thing (TMGT) effect and conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study aims to investigate the direct and indirect curvilinear effects of spiritual leadership (SL) on employee role-based performance (RBP). Design/methodology/approach This study used a multi-study design combining an experimental study with 136 participants and a time-lagged, multisource field survey of 216 hospitality sector employees. Findings Findings collectively demonstrate that SL exhibits an inverted U-shaped curvilinear relationship with employee RBP, both directly and indirectly through employee resilience. Practical implications Theoretically, the “sweet spot” of SL challenges linear resource–performance assumptions, suggesting that TMGT and CORs theory must account for how resilience shapes the point at which SL ceases to enhance employee RBP. In practice, hospitality managers should calibrate SL to a level that strengthens employee resilience and supports effective performance across their roles. Beyond an optimal level, increasing leadership intensity may weaken these benefits, thus highlighting the importance of balanced leadership and resilience-supportive practices in hospitality management. Originality/value The study advanced hospitality leadership literature by integrating two complementary designs and providing novel evidence of the curvilinear effects of SL on employee RBP as well as the underlying psychological mechanism through which these nonlinear effects occur, thus presenting a multidimensional outcome rarely examined in SL research.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Tell me about yourself and I might recommend you: a motivation-based explanation of crowdlending investors’ customer citizenship behavior☆
abstract: Competition among entrepreneurial funding platforms has made it more important than ever to attract and retain investors to ensure the sustainability of entrepreneurial ecosystems. In this context, investor recommendations are a key mechanism to generate trust in crowdlending platforms. This paper investigates the existence of necessary and sufficient conditions that explain investor recommendations of crowdlending platforms and explores how the motivations behind investor behavior are linked to investor recommendations of these platforms. Necessary condition analysis (NCA) and qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) were performed using data on 83 investors. Of the intrinsic/self-oriented motivations considered in the analysis, only satisfaction emerged as an individual in-degree necessary condition from the NCA. The analysis also confirmed the synergistic effects of intrinsic/self-oriented and extrinsic/other-oriented motivations as sufficient conditions for explaining investor behavior. Nonetheless, such behavior can still be explained exclusively by intrinsic/self-oriented conditions. The study enriches the knowledge of how investor motivations explain the sustainability of platforms that provide alternative forms of financing for entrepreneurs.

title: Does Biodiversity Risk Matter to Capital Markets? New Evidence from China
VAT Sharing, Fiscal Incentives, and Corporate Financialization
abstract: Under fiscal decentralization, local government interventions driven by tax-sharing incentives are key to understanding corporate financialization. By taking China’s 2016 VAT revenue-sharing reform as a quasi-natural experiment and utilizing panel data of A-share manufacturing firms covering the 2012–2021 period, we employ an intensity DID design to examine its effect. The empirical results demonstrate that a higher local VAT share significantly inhibits corporate financialization, and this core conclusion remains stable across robustness checks. Mechanism tests reveal that strengthened fiscal incentives lead local governments to increase credit support and relax environmental enforcement, thereby mitigating financialization. This effect is more prominent for enterprises with high external financing demands, high-pollution industries, and fiscally stressed regions. The study provides insights into mitigating financialization and enhancing VAT sharing design.

title: Can artificial intelligence accelerate technological progress? Researchers' perspectives on AI in manufacturing and materials science
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) raises expectations of substantial increases in rates of technological progress, but such anticipations are often not connected to detailed ground-level studies of AI use in innovation processes. Accordingly, it remains unclear how and to what extent AI can accelerate innovation. To help to fill this gap, we explore and assess results from 32 interviews with U.S.-based academic manufacturing and materials sciences researchers experienced with AI and machine learning (ML) techniques. We found that AI was primarily used for modeling of materials and manufacturing processes, facilitating cheaper and more rapid search of design spaces for materials and manufacturing processes alike. Benefits included cost, time, and computation savings in technology development. However, AI/ML tools were unreliable outside design spaces for which dense data were already available; they required skilled and judicious application in tandem with older research techniques; and concerns were raised about the potential to detrimentally circumvent opportunities for disruptive theoretical advancement. Based on these results, we suggest there is reason for optimism about acceleration in sustaining innovations through the use of AI/ML; but that support for conventional empirical, computational, and theoretical research is required to maintain the likelihood of further disruptive advances in manufacturing and materials.

title: How to craft a mission? A Theory of Action for the strategic public management of mission-oriented innovation policy
abstract: This paper explores the role of strategic public management within mission-oriented innovation policy. While recent scholarship has emphasised multiple aspects of missions, the distinct relevance of strategic public management in their implementation remains under-explored. To address this gap, the paper performs two complementary tasks. First, it uses a qualitative meta-synthesis of the relevant innovation literature to articulate a new Theory of Action for the analysis of missioncraft: namely, the institutional work public managers perform to create or maintain (disrupt) institutional logics supporting (hinder) their effective implementation. Second, it leverages a pre-study of the extant literature to illustrate the Theory of Action with three historical vignettes showing how the ToA can be applied at different scales and under different institutional logics (US' DARPA; China's NEV Plan programme; and EU's RIS3). Overall, the paper argues that the implementation of mission-oriented innovation policy requires public managers to adopt three critical strategic roles: i) enabling strategic learning across the public sector organisations leading the mission; ii) enabling dynamic accountability in the portfolio of projects supported by the mission; and iii) enabling collaborative innovation among the societal actors partaking the mission. By shifting the focus on the micro-foundations of mission implementation from structural underpinnings (i.e., legal, organisational, managerial) to agentic functions (i.e., strategic roles), the paper provides a new diagnostic lens for innovation policy research and practice – reflecting whether and how public managers can support mission-oriented innovation policy in light of the context-specific opportunities and constraints they face in their institutional work.

title: Design anthropology for transforming power relations in societal transitions
Executive agencies in developing countries: the case of the parastatal organizations in Suriname
Symptom-level associations between childhood trauma and academic defeat: A network analysis of 11,031 Chinese adolescents
abstract: Background Academic defeat represents a critical construct associated with mental health outcomes in East Asian societies with high-stakes competition. However, conventional models obscure symptom-level mechanisms linking childhood trauma to this sense of failure. This study investigated the topological architecture connecting childhood trauma to academic defeat and identified specific bridge pathways. Methods This cross-sectional study included 11,031 adolescents recruited via multi-stage stratified cluster sampling in Shandong Province, China. The Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form and a culturally adapted Defeat Scale were used to assess trauma experiences and academic defeat, respectively. A regularized partial correlation network was estimated via a Gaussian graphical model to map symptom associations. Bridge centrality indices were calculated to identify nodes connecting the constructs, and the Network Comparison Test was used to evaluate structural and expected influence invariance across genders and school types. Results The self-perceived symptom of “Learning failure” exhibited the highest expected influence within the network. “Emotional abuse” functioned as the primary bridge connecting trauma to academic defeat, specifically linking to “Powerless”. “Emotional neglect” served as a robust secondary bridge, strongly associated with “Successful person” and “Basically a winner”. Furthermore, significant structural differences existed between male and female networks, specifically regarding the pathway between “Powerless” and “Emotional abuse”. Conclusions The present study delineates the complex relationship between childhood trauma and academic defeat. Future efforts should focus on targeted interventions that address these identified bridge and central symptoms to effectively disrupt the mechanisms underlying this sense of failure.

title: Motivated to exhaustion? Public service motivation, curvilinear strain, and the buffer of collaborative culture
abstract: Public service motivation (PSM) is widely treated as a resource that strengthens engagement, yet excessive motivation may yield diminishing returns. Integrating the job demands-resources model, conservation of resources theory, and the too-much-of-a-good-thing logic, this study tests a curvilinear relationship between PSM and job exhaustion, and the moderating role of collaborative culture. Using a two-wave survey of 408 Korean public servants with a one-month lag, hierarchical regressions identify a U-shaped pattern: exhaustion declines at low-to-moderate PSM but rises beyond a threshold. Collaborative culture significantly flattens this curve, indicating that supportive, collective norms mitigate PSM-related strain at very high levels of PSM. The findings challenge the assumption that PSM is uniformly beneficial, recasting PSM as a conditional resource that can operate as a demand at high levels. The study clarifies when PSM is sustainable and positions collaboration as an actionable boundary condition, yielding implications for motivation theory and for the collaborative organization of public service.

title: Advances in microchannel flow boiling heat transfer: mechanisms and performance optimization
abstract: Microchannel flow boiling has emerged as a promising technology for thermal management of electronic devices due to its high heat transfer coefficient, low pumping power, and compact cooling architecture. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in microchannel flow boiling heat transfer and performance optimization strategies. The fundamental mechanisms governing microchannel flow boiling are first summarized with emphasis on bubble dynamics, microscale confinement effects, interfacial phase change, and thin film evaporation. Then the effects of channel geometry, surface modification, and working fluid modification on heat transfer performance are further analyzed by elucidating how these strategies regulate the underlying mechanisms of microchannel flow boiling. Furthermore, emerging optimization strategies are discussed in terms of hybrid active passive regulation, coordinated regulation of multiple boiling mechanisms, and artificial intelligence (AI) assisted prediction and optimization. Representative approaches include topology-optimized microchannel structures, adaptive shape memory alloy (SMA)-based regulation, jet microchannel coupled cooling, and AI-assisted prediction and optimization methods. The practical limitations of existing strategies are also discussed in terms of manufacturability, durability, operational stability, cost, packaging compatibility, and system level integration. Finally, the current challenges and future research directions in microchannel flow boiling are outlined. This review provides guidance for the design and optimization of next generation thermal management systems for high power electronic and energy systems.

title: From Destruction to Reconstruction: Substrate-Driven Biosynthesis of Antioxidants from Antibiotic Residues in Hyperthermophilic Composting
abstract: Abstract The accumulation of tetracycline (TC) in organic fertilizers poses severe risks by fostering antibiotic resistance in soil ecosystems. Hyperthermophilic composting effectively mitigates these threats, achieving nearly complete TC removal via thermal selection. Although previous studies have widely characterized the catabolic degradation routes of TC, we propose a novel transformation pathway in which TC-derived intermediates are redirected into secondary metabolism to synthesize antioxidant alkaloids and flavonoids. Integrated abiotic–biotic controls first demonstrated that while heat initiates breakdown, hyperthermophilic microbiota drive the subsequent deep transformation and diversification of products. FT-ICR-MS revealed that this process is underpinned by substrate restructuring, where recalcitrant compounds are depolymerized into bioenergetically favorable low-molecular-weight organic matter (LMW-OM). Cross-feeding assays confirmed that this accessible substrate pool significantly enhances cometabolic efficiency compared to conventional composting-derived substrates. Mechanistically, multiomics indicated that LMW-OM elevates intracellular NADH and ATP within the Thermus-dominated community, shifting metabolism from maintenance to active biosynthesis. Consequently, TC intermediates acting as structural mimics of endogenous aromatic precursors are recruited into these energized pathways to generate antioxidants. Crucially, diverting residues into anabolic networks eliminates the selective pressure exerted by intermediates, explaining the extensive attenuation of the antibiotic resistance genes. This work highlights pivotal substrate-microbe interplay, offering a new paradigm for converting antibiotic-laden waste into functional bio-organic fertilizers.

title: Microbial Bioenergetics and Ecology Govern the Coupled Biogeochemical Cycling of Arsenic/Antimony and Macronutrients
abstract: Abstract Arsenic (As) and antimony (Sb) are toxic metalloids whose biogeochemical cycles are strongly influenced by carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and sulfur (S) through microbially mediated coupled transformations. However, the mechanistic basis of these coupled processes remains poorly understood. In this Review, we synthesize current advances in the interconnected cycling and elucidate their thermodynamic and ecological foundations. Redox-sensitive As, Sb, C, N, and S species serve as electron donors and acceptors in microbial respiratory chains, and the combination of their redox half-reactions results in the coupled cycles. A redox-ladder framework delineates the theoretical electron flow and thermodynamically feasible coupling combinations. Many combinations have been observed in the environments-for instance, NO3– reduction to N2 coupled with As(III)/Sb(III) oxidation. Their realization also depends on microorganisms harboring key genes (e.g., aioA and arrA). The redox-ladder further predicts novel coupling processes, such as As(III)/Sb(III) oxidation coupled to N2O reduction to N2. We finally emphasize the need for quantitative biogeochemical models within global change scenarios.
