On the Value of Improved Forecasting for Specialty Crop Producers Through Intra‐Season Supply Allocations
abstract: ABSTRACT How to manage harvest and storage of agricultural products has been one of the long‐lasting questions in agricultural economics. We study the value of improved forecast accuracy for the producers in the context of intra‐seasonal supply allocation, particularly for specialty crops with multiple harvest cycles within a season. We first explore how the forecast accuracy affects intra‐seasonal storage decisions. We then derive the expression for the marginal value of the improved forecast accuracy and show that the gains from the improvement in the forecast accuracy occur by shifting the optimal storage choices to those under certainty (i.e., the state is revealed) from those under uncertainty. Finally, we provide numerical illustrations on how the value of the improved forecast accuracy for the producers differs across different degrees of market power showing that relative gains from the improvement are larger when the market is more competitive. We conclude by drawing broader implications highlighting the importance of the interaction among information, storage and market structure.

title: Early career effects of entering the labor market during higher education expansion
abstract: Abstract We evaluate the labor market effects of an increasing supply of high-skilled labor, resulting from a higher education expansion at established German universities. Exploiting variation in exposure across regions and cohorts, we estimate early career effects for labor market entrants. We find that high-skilled wages decline initially, particularly in non-graduate jobs, but recover over the first 5 years of experience. For graduate job takers, we even report positive wage effects after 5 years. We explain the dynamics of the effects by the interplay of several mechanisms: immediate supply effects, recovery through regional mobility, and increased productivity of graduate jobs.

title: The value of a statistical life year
abstract: Abstract Embedded in the value of a statistical life (VSL) is a stream of valuations of each expected year of life. The value of a statistical life year (VSLY) has a policy-relevant role analogous to the VSL, except that it monetizes risks to short periods of life extension. This article reviews previous studies and reports new labor market estimates of the average VSLY and the variation of these values with age using two methods—inferring the average VSLY based on estimates of the VSL and a new method that provides direct empirical estimates of the valuation of a discounted life year. The direct estimates of the VSLY yield larger values than the constructed estimates. The VSLY based on fatality rates by industry and occupation is $600,000 to $800,000 at a 3% interest rate. Estimates based on age-adjusted fatality rates are somewhat lower. The discount rate used in assessing the VSLY has a pivotal effect on the estimated VSLY. The VSLY is substantially lower in the absence of discounting and more than doubled at a discount rate of 10%. Failure to use a positive discount rate greatly understates the VSLY. The article also reviews previous VSLY studies as well as estimates of the discount rate for years of life expectancy.

title: High Frequency Measurement of Consumer Price Inflation Using Scanner Data
Modelling the macroeconomic impact of Brazil's ecological transformation plan: a stock-flow consistent approach
abstract: In 2023, the Brazilian government launched the Ecological Transformation Plan (ETP), a new development strategy aimed at promoting environmentally sustainable economic growth while enhancing productivity and social equity. This paper evaluates the macroeconomic impacts of the ETP's financial policy mix, by developing a stock-flow consistent model. The analysis focuses on representing the policy mix embedded in the ETP—particularly its financial instruments—and evaluating its implications for investment, growth, and macroeconomic stability. A key contribution of the paper is the explicit modelling of financing mechanisms designed to mitigate currency risk, a structural constraint that affects many EMDEs and limits the scalability of low-carbon investments. By incorporating these features into an SFC framework, the paper provides new insights into how financial structures and policy interventions interact with real economic dynamics. Simulations through 2030 indicate that the ETP is expansionary, with projected GDP growth rising up to 1.6% and the creation of 360,000 to 900,000 new jobs. While the plan improves the primary fiscal balance by increasing tax revenues, it introduces specific trade-offs: the reduction in unemployment may prompt the Central Bank to raise the Selic rate to curb inflation, and increased demand for capital goods is expected to widen the current account deficit by 0.2–0.4 p.p. of GDP.

title: Cross-Border Venture Capital in the Semiconductor Industry: Knowledge Spillover or Capital Deepening?
How Do Energy Transition Policies Affect Corporate Sustainability? Evidence from China
From Algorithmic Trading to Generative AI: Artificial Intelligence, Systemic Risk, and the Transformation of Financial Markets
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence can improve financial information processing while also synchronizing decisions, concentrating operational dependence, and accelerating market feedback. Yet evidence on these effects is divided among market microstructure, machine‐learning risk analytics, algorithmic intermediation, and generative AI. We integrate these literatures using 769 English‐language articles, reviews, and book chapters retrieved from OpenAlex for 1990– July 29, 2026, bibliometric performance and relational analyses, and structured content coding of 96 studies. Publication growth accelerated after 2021, but collaboration remained fragmented and the 2023–2026 frontier shifted sharply toward generative AI and governance. Bibliographic‐coupling assignments were stable to stricter thresholds and the exclusion of partial‐year 2026 records, although weak cluster separation cautions against treating algorithmic communities as theories. Content synthesis shows that automation usually improves normal‐state liquidity and signal extraction; systemic risk emerges when common models, objectives, infrastructures, or narratives correlate actions and meet thin risk‐bearing capacity. Evidence is strongest for average market‐quality effects and weakest for vendor‐commonality, agent autonomy, and equilibrium feedback. We propose an architecture–use–amplifier–outcome framework and ten falsifiable designs for identifying when AI creates resilience rather than scalable fragility.

title: The Evolving Role of Finance in Environmental Strategy: Integrating Climate, Sustainable, and Biodiversity Finance
abstract: ABSTRACT The literature on climate finance, sustainable finance, and biodiversity finance has expanded rapidly over the past two decades, yet it remains conceptually fragmented and often organized around specific mechanisms, risks, or policy initiatives. This paper provides a systematic and integrative review of this evolving field by combining bibliometric, thematic, and qualitative analyses of 1228 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2007 and 2025. The results document a progressive broadening of research focus, from climate‐related risk pricing and disclosure, to firm‐level sustainability strategies, and more recently to natural capital and ecosystem‐oriented financial mechanisms. Building on these patterns, the paper introduces the strategic integration pathway of Climate, Sustainable, and Biodiversity Finance (CSBF), a conceptual framework that organizes the literature around three dominant and coexisting logics of financial–managerial engagement: defensive, strategic, and regenerative. Rather than treating these domains as sequential stages or isolated subfields, the framework highlights increasing depth of integration between finance, management, and environmental systems. By clarifying how the role of finance evolves under tightening ecological constraints, the study contributes to theory development in sustainable finance and provides a structured foundation for future research, managerial decision‐making, and policy design.

title: The Visible Hand, the Invisible Hand, and the Firm's Own Hand What Propels ESG Engagement in Chinese Companies
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper surveys the empirical literature on the antecedents of corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) engagement in China, distinguishing substantive ESG actions, ESG disclosure, externally assigned ESG performance, and symbolic or reputational responses. Synthesizing 126 studies published between 2004 and 2024 in leading journals on the UTD, FT and ABS lists, we develop a tripartite analytical model in which forces at the government, market and firm levels jointly determine ESG behavior through three interaction logics, namely mutual reinforcement, substitution and contingency. The evidence identifies regulatory pressure, policy incentives, state ownership and political connections, together with media scrutiny, product market competition, institutional investors and customer demands, as well as organizational resources, governance arrangements and strategic orientation, as the principal antecedents of ESG engagement. Their relative importance varies systematically over time and across regions, industries, and ownership types, although changes in research attention do not by themselves establish a transition in Chinese ESG governance. We further document considerable theoretical fragmentation, as institutional, stakeholder, and resource‐based perspectives are widely applied but seldom combined. The survey concludes with an agenda for future research covering meta‐analytic validation, firm‐level mechanisms, heterogeneity across ESG dimensions, digitalization and cross‐country comparison.

title: A Bibliometric Review of Digital Currency Research: An International Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on the Web of Science database, this study reviews the digital currency papers published between 2016 and 2025. Using bibliometric analysis, we document a substantial increase in research output in this field, reflecting growing academic and policy interest. The United States and China emerge as the two most productive countries in digital currency research, with China taking a leading position in publication volume after the launch of its central bank digital currency (CBDC) in 2019. The leading journals publishing digital currency research are Finance Research Letters , International Review of Financial Analysis , and Economics Letters . The most extensively studied topics include Bitcoin price dynamics, the risk‐return characteristics of digital currencies, and CBDC development. Building on our bibliometric evidence, we further identify several avenues for future research, including corporate finance and governance, financial intermediation, financial inclusion, digital currency ecosystem and financial stability.

title: An Experimental Study on the Effect of Knowledge on Idea Generation and Idea Selection
Identification of Relationship Lending in Bank–Borrower Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Relationship lending refers to lending based on close bank–borrower relationships, expected to increase credit availability and support real economic activity. This paper proposes the ST‐B filter, a novel framework identifying significant ties in temporal bipartite networks. Applying our method to Japanese financial data (1977–2021), relationship lending comprises about 10%–35% of total lending and is associated with 33% larger loan volume than transaction lending. Our method uniquely enables the analysis of relationship lending using only transaction data, without requiring detailed information on bank–borrower relationships.
journal_name: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics

title: Can we be serious? A comment on Mata on genre
abstract: There are many lenses through which to analyze the history of economics, the number growing with scholars’ increasingly expansive conceptions of the field over the last few decades. This article offers a brief and affirmative comment on Tiago Mata’s discussion of the use of the concept of genres in history of economics and its application to the study of works that fall under the heading of “popular economics.” Thinking in terms of genre—which draws us to questions of form, style, and purpose—offers a useful vantage point from which to explore the history of economics, one that encourages us to think in a different set of ways about what is being done and how and why, and the implications for understanding the history of economics.
journal_name: The European Journal of the History of Economic Thought

title: The welfare effects of input price discrimination under endogenous horizontal differentiation
Sustainable finance literacy predicts investment behavior beyond general financial literacy: Evidence from two representative samples
journal_name: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance

title: Institutional Quality and Financial Stability in MENA’s Dual Banking Systems: A Machine Learning Approach
journal_name: Research in International Business and Finance

title: First In, First Out? Birth Order and Next-Generation Engagement in Family Firms
abstract: Research shows that next-generation engagement in the family business is important for the business’s long-term survival. However, the literature has neglected how differences among children could explain their career choices in the family business. We address this gap by drawing on birth order theory to examine differences in three career choices of the next-generation: joining the family business, holding a managerial position, and leaving the family business. Using a sample from Sweden, we employ family-stratified hazard models and show that later-borns are more likely to join the family business as their initial career choice compared to earlier-born siblings. However, when the next-generation joins the family business, later-borns are less likely to hold managerial positions in the family business and more likely to leave the family business. We conduct several mechanism tests explaining our hypotheses and run additional robustness tests to support our results. This study advances the research on next-generation engagement in family firms.

title: Generative Search: Evidence from a Large-Scale Field Experiment
abstract: Generative search is an emerging search paradigm that integrates Generative AI (GenAI) into traditional search engines by presenting users with AI-generated responses before conventional search results. Whereas keyword-based search requires consumers to translate their underlying needs into effective keyword queries, generative search lets users express those intentions directly in natural language, a shift made possible by GenAI’s new mode of information presentation. This shift moves the consumer-search engine interaction upstream to the stage of problem formulation, rendering empirically observable a previously hidden phase of search behavior: the mapping from problem formulation to keyword articulation. Yet, it remains empirically unknown whether generative search increases consumer purchases and how search behavior changes when it can begin from expressed intent rather than keywords. Using a large-scale field experiment conducted on Meituan, a leading Chinese technology platform, this paper provides empirical evidence on the effectiveness of generative search. We find that generative search significantly increases consumer purchases. Further analysis reveals that generative search facilitates more effective and diverse keyword queries and reduces exploratory browsing and clicking, while concentrating evaluation within relevant categories and merchants. The empirical evidence is most consistent with a mechanism in which AI-generated answers provide information about consumers’ underlying needs, while also expanding awareness of relevant attributes and shifting attention toward more relevant categories. These findings provide empirical insights for future consumer search models that allow search to originate at the intention-expressing stage. This paper was accepted by Raphael Thomadsen, marketing. Funding: Financial support from the Ministry of Education – Singapore [Grant A-8001730-00-00] is gratefully acknowledged. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02458 .

title: Direct and Indirect Effects of Transparency Regulation
Policy‐Level Environmental Architecture and Corporate Renewable‐Energy Transition
abstract: ABSTRACT Corporate renewable‐energy transition is often assessed through climate commitments, ESG scores, or carbon indicators, although these measures may not reveal firms' capacity to translate formal policies into operational change. Using a newly assembled point‐in‐time panel of European listed companies drawn from the STOXX universe over 2015–2025, this study constructs a holistic environmental‐management architecture score comprising resource/nature and climate/energy management pillars. The common estimation samples contain 1161 firm‐year observations from 264 firms for the 1‐year horizon and 869 observations from 215 firms for the 2‐year horizon. Firm and fiscal‐year fixed‐effects models relate environmental‐management architecture in fiscal year to subsequent changes in renewable‐energy use over and , complemented by pillar‐level and component‐level decompositions, alternative fixed‐effects structures, and sector exclusions. The holistic architecture score is positive but imprecisely estimated. Resource/nature management is positively associated with subsequent renewable‐energy improvement at both horizons, whereas climate/energy formalization is not. Water‐efficiency policy is marginally significant at the 1‐year horizon and statistically significant at the 2‐year horizon. The findings show that formal environmental policies do not carry uniform information about operational transition and highlight the value of examining policy domains and implementation‐related organizational routines separately.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Gender Diversity at the Innovation Core and Environmental Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper estimates the effect of gender diversity on firm‐level environmental innovation. We use a large Spanish panel data and construct an inverse‐covariance‐weighted environmental innovation index. Identification comes from persistent within‐firm increases in women's representation, measured relative to a 2‐year rolling pre‐event baseline. Across several difference‐in‐differences estimators, a 5% increase in women's share of in‐house R&D personnel is associated with an increase in environmental innovation of 1.2–1.6 points. This corresponds to approximately 3%–4% of the sample mean and builds gradually over the years, consistent with a durable reorientation of innovation effort rather than a transient compositional change. The corresponding evidence for the overall female employment share is weaker and estimator‐sensitive. Empirical Bayes analysis shows that firms with larger internal underrepresentation of women in R&D have lower environmental innovation. The evidence suggests that the relevant margin is not simply gender diversity in the firm, but gender diversity inside the innovation‐producing core.

title: Generative AI Disclosure in Advertising: From Intent- to Production-Based Disclosure
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming advertising production and introducing new forms of disclosure at the point of exposure. Existing research treats disclosure primarily as a cue signaling persuasive intent, yet GenAI disclosures increasingly communicate how content was produced rather than why it was created. This paper reconceptualizes disclosure in AI-mediated advertising by positioning GenAI disclosure as a signal of production conditions. Integrating signaling theory, source credibility theory, the persuasion knowledge model, and the heuristic–systematic model, the paper develops a conceptual framework that differentiates declarative, regulatory, and infrastructural disclosure as distinct rendering conditions. The framework proposes that GenAI disclosure influences consumer evaluations through two complementary inferential pathways: perceived source attribution and production-based agent knowledge, defined as consumers’ beliefs about how persuasive content was generated and what those production processes imply for evaluating the persuasion agent. It further specifies how consumers’ motivation and ability shape the likelihood of heuristic versus systematic processing. The paper advances advertising theory by explaining how disclosure operates when its primary referent shifts from persuasive intent to production conditions and by providing a framework for understanding why similar disclosure cues may generate divergent evaluative responses across consumers, contexts, and forms of GenAI use.

title: Should Ads Be Assertive? A Meta-Analytic Review of the Effects of Assertive Language on Perceived Freedom Threat, State Reactance, and Persuasion Outcomes
abstract: Advertising messages often use assertive language to capture consumer attention and drive behavioral compliance, yet empirical evidence for its effectiveness remains inconclusive and contradictory across studies and contexts. This meta-analytic review synthesized 142 samples examining the effects of assertive language in advertising messages on perceived freedom threat, state reactance, and persuasion outcomes. Drawing on psychological reactance theory, we used meta-analytic structural equation modeling (MASEM) to conduct the first test in the reactance literature of a serial mediation model in which assertive language first increases perceived freedom threat, which subsequently heightens state reactance, ultimately reducing persuasive effectiveness. Overall, assertive language significantly increased perceived freedom threat (d = 0.72) and state reactance (d = 0.39), while demonstrating a small but significant negative effect on persuasion outcomes (d = −0.08). Importantly, MASEM provided evidence that the effect of assertive language on persuasion outcomes was serially mediated through perceived threat to freedom and state reactance. Moderation analyses revealed that advertising domain significantly moderated the effect on state reactance, with nonprofit contexts eliciting stronger reactance responses than for-profit contexts. These findings clarify the mechanism of psychological reactance in advertising and provide clear guidance for advertisers on when and why to avoid assertive language.

title: Income inequality and entrepreneurial motivations: A cross-country analysis of the moderating roles of trade openness and individual capital
How firms bundle R&D and marketing capabilities for innovation: a systematic review and contingency model
abstract: Purpose This study systematically reviews 25 years of research on the R&D–marketing strategy nexus (2000–2025) and proposes a contingency model explaining when and why specific capability configurations enhance innovation performance. Design/methodology/approach We identified 140 peer-reviewed studies through a PRISMA-compliant search of Scopus, filtered by the ABS Academic Journal Guide. Each study was coded using the Antecedents–Decisions–Outcomes/Theories–Contexts–Methods (ADO-TCM) framework. Bibliometric mapping and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling complemented the deductive coding with inductive identification of thematic clusters. A co-word robustness check validated the LDA solution. Findings Marketing capability, network relationships and technology capability rank as the most frequently studied antecedents, with organisational structure and environmental dynamism close behind; market orientation, which earlier work placed at the centre, is coded in fewer than one study in ten. Marketing-strategy and product-development decisions dominate the corpus almost equally, while temporal sequencing of orchestration choices remains unstudied. Two in five studies invoke no explicit theory; evidence concentrates in the USA and East Asia and in manufacturing or multi-industry samples, with services almost absent. Integrating ADO–TCM patterns with LDA clusters, we derive three testable propositions: a turbulence–agility mechanism, a digital–complementarity mechanism and a legitimacy–consistency mechanism. We introduce the concept of integration intelligence, the meta-capability through which managers diagnose which orchestration configuration fits their current competitive context. Originality/value The paper reframes R&D–marketing coordination as capability orchestration rather than functional integration, fusing the Dynamic Capabilities View with Resource Orchestration Theory. The resulting contingency model moves beyond the question of whether integration improves performance toward specifying which configurations improve performance under which conditions, offering both a theoretical architecture and a research agenda organised around generative AI, platform ecosystems and sustainability transitions.

title: The personalization–privacy paradox in social media advertising: a cross-national study of ad attitudes and eWOM
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore how advertising personalization and perceived intrusiveness influence consumers' attitudes toward social media ads and their subsequent electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) behaviors. Using the privacy calculus theory and the theory of planned behavior, we examine whether personalized ads boost positive attitudes and whether intrusiveness diminishes them. Additionally, we analyze how these attitudes translate into positive or negative eWOM, comparing three EU countries (Poland, Portugal and Sweden) that operate under GDPR but differ in digital literacy and privacy concerns. Design/methodology/approach We conducted an online survey of Instagram users in three target countries. After data cleaning, the final samples included N = 337 (Poland), 200 (Portugal) and 196 (Sweden). Respondents rated established multi-item scales for ad personalization, intrusiveness, ad attitude and positive/negative eWOM intent. Data were analyzed using multi-group structural equation modeling to test the hypothesized model and compare effects across countries. Findings The results consistently indicate that higher personalization fosters more positive attitudes toward ads, while greater perceived intrusiveness results in less positive attitudes. Positive ad attitudes, in turn, significantly boost intentions for positive eWOM across all countries. Notably, strong ad attitudes also predict higher intentions for negative eWOM, suggesting ambivalent reactions to personalization. Additionally, perceived intrusiveness diminishes the positive impact of personalization on ad attitudes in Portugal and Sweden (moderation confirmed), but this moderating effect was not significant in Poland. Originality/value This research makes a novel contribution by integrating marketing and information systems frameworks and empirically testing them across diverse national contexts. Integrating privacy calculus theory and the theory of planned behavior frameworks, it addresses both the positive (personalization) and negative (intrusiveness) sides of targeted advertising, a distinction often omitted in single-country studies. To our knowledge, this is among the first cross-country studies to compare these effects within a unified model; by examining Poland, Portugal and Sweden together, the paper offers new insights into how cultural and regulatory contexts shape the personalization–privacy paradox in eWOM outcomes.

title: Beyond the classroom: dialogic action for sustainability accounting education and practice
Corporate social responsibility and investors with multiple blockholdings: a monitoring capacity perspective
Consumer vulnerability in artificial intelligence-driven marketing: A paradox theory lens
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing through hyper-personalization, predictive analytics and enhanced customer experience, yet its ethical implications for consumer vulnerability remain undertheorized. We apply a paradox theory lens to identify four tensions in AI-driven marketing: Diversity (included versus excluded), Data (safeguarded versus exploited), Dignity (empowered versus dependent), and Development (informed versus misinformed). We advance a conceptual framework situating these tensions within key boundary conditions (consumer agency, marketer intentionality, and AI opacity) that determine whether AI alleviates or exacerbates consumer vulnerability. In doing so, we extend marketing scholarship on AI-driven marketing, consumer vulnerability, and inclusion by theorizing AI as a relational, dual-sided agent rather than a uniformly empowering or exploitative one, built on a both/and paradox framing. We also translate the framework into strategic guidelines, CARE (Control, Aim, Reveal, and Empathy), that encapsulate our framework’s boundary conditions and dimensions to help practitioners and policymakers act on these tensions in practice.

title: When luxury brands roar: the effect of animal logo types on consumers’ luxury consumption
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how animal logo types of luxury brands influence consumers’ luxury consumption. Design/methodology/approach Based on the Stereotype Content Model, this research investigates whether competent (vs warm) animal logos influence consumers’ luxury consumption through perceived dominance, and how this effect is moderated by message appeal (competitive vs cooperative). The investigation employs a multi-method approach with seven interrelated studies: an exploratory study, an eye-tracking study and five controlled experiments. Findings The results demonstrate that consumers prefer luxury brands featuring competent animal logos over those with warm logos. This preference stems from the ability of competent animal logos to better fulfill consumers’ psychological need for perceived dominance. This effect, however, is appeal-dependent: within cooperative appeals, animal logo type does not significantly influence perceived dominance. Research limitations/implications Moving beyond a focus on animal symbolism, this study centers on visual design expression as the key driver of meaning in animal logos. It examines how such expression shapes consumer perceptions and behavior. This extends the Stereotype Content Model to animal representations in luxury branding and clarifies how consumers decide on luxury purchases. Practical implications This research offers practical implications for luxury goods companies regarding the strategic use of animal logos to drive luxury consumption and enhance brand strategy effectiveness. Originality/value While animal symbolism is widely used in branding, and animal logos are prevalent in luxury contexts, the influence of visual design expression in animal logos on consumer perception and decision-making remains underexplored. This study addresses this significant gap in luxury marketing research.

title: Modern Slavery in Supply Chains: A Framing Perspective on Managerial Responses to Transparency Legislation
abstract: ABSTRACT Innovative legislation aspires for an extra‐jurisdictional effect on modern slavery in supply chains through increased transparency. Evidence to date suggests that firms are not rising to this challenge, and, if anything, mandatory reporting practices are coalescing around superficial reports decoupled from policy objectives. To decide how the regulatory regime should best be adapted, it is important to understand not just the organizational‐level response but also the underlying managerial attitudes and behavior on which substantive practical action depends. The study utilized a photo elicitation method with 47 managers drawn from eight large UK construction firms. Framing theory was utilized to reveal four distinct managerial mindsets, each with different implications for policy and practice. These variants suggest that a one‐size‐fits‐all policy approach is suboptimal. Policy combining rewards and penalties, tailored to each framing group, is likely to be the most expedient in quickly improving managerial behavior. The existence of inconsistent framing within firms suggests that strategic policies are not being effectively embedded in managerial practice. In turn, this limits the impact that focal firms have in improving labor practices across multiple tiers of their supply chains. Reporting entities should not be treated as cohesive, unitary entities by stakeholders.

title: Adaptive management control systems in operations: the reconfiguration of control mechanisms on the shop floor
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the complexity and dynamics of assembly line managers' management control systems. It examines which mechanisms comprise these systems and how their relevance and configuration change as managers tackle different productivity-related control problems on the shop floor. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an abductive single case study approach, drawing on interview, observational and archival data from a global automotive supplier. Building on complexity theory and management control research, it analyses line managers' control problems on a U-shaped assembly line. Findings The study identifies three recurrent workforce-related control problems (workforce assignment, managing process interruptions and motivating the team) and shows how five types of management control mechanisms (administrative, cultural, cybernetic, planning and reward) combine into distinct configurations around each control problem. These configurations shift as managers' attention moves between control problems, representing dynamics that can be interpreted through the lens of a complex adaptive system. Practical implications By demonstrating how line managers combine and reconfigure control mechanisms across recurring control problems, this study offers actionable insights for line manager training and for senior managers seeking to support shop floor productivity. Originality/value This study interprets management control systems in operations as complex adaptive systems and introduces the notion of control problem dynamics, showing how shop floor productivity management emerges through the co-evolution of control mechanisms and the control problems they address.
journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Old and connected versus young and creative: Networks and the diffusion of new scientific ideas
From Policy Neglect to Research Agenda: Administrative Burdens and Donor‐Conceived Mobilization
abstract: ABSTRACT Donor‐conceived adults are a growing population, mobilizing against the very regulatory arrangements that determined the terms into which they were conceived. In Canada and the United States, where donor conception remains persistently under‐regulated, gamete donation policy has historically prioritized the presumed needs of donors, recipient parents, and fertility clinics, structuring regulation around treatment access and donor supply rather than the long‐term interests of those conceived. The result is a population that bears disproportionate administrative burdens and is now mobilizing through advocacy organizations, legal claims, and the pathways consumer DNA testing has made possible. Yet donor‐conceived adults remain largely outside the scope of policy scholarship. This paper argues that donor conception offers a theoretically distinctive site for the study of administrative burden, policy feedback, and the social construction of target populations. The paper proposes a research agenda organized around the politics of administratively produced populations and the deliberate distribution of administrative burden through policy design.

title: Psychological safety, motivations and change-oriented organizational citizenship behaviour in emergency managers
abstract: Fostering change-oriented organizational citizenship behaviour (CO-OCB) is critical for resilience-building in the public sector, yet the psychological mechanisms driving such behaviour among emergency managers remain underexplored. Drawing on a survey of 869 public employees from emergency management agencies in China, this study examines how psychological safety, creative self-efficacy (CSE), and public service motivation (PSM) influence CO-OCB and tests the moderating role of work autonomy. Results reveal that psychological safety and PSM positively predict CO-OCB, whereas CSE unexpectedly suppresses the effect of psychological safety. Notably, work autonomy moderates the impacts of CSE and PSM on CO-OCB. These findings reveal how psychological safety shapes change-oriented behaviour through distinct but interrelated competence-related and motivational mechanisms within bureaucratic contexts. This study advances public-sector innovation theory by uncovering the nuanced role of psychological safety and by emphasizing the importance of public service motivation in enhancing organizational resilience during institutional reforms and crises.

title: Judge, butler, and tool: algorithmic imaginaries and practices of Chinese parent vloggers of autistic children on Douyin
abstract: Disability-related new media practices have increasingly attracted scholarly attention. However, existing research often frames user agency in these practices through a binary lens of either ‘empowerment’ or ‘alienation’, insufficiently capturing the complexities of their entanglements with digital technologies. Drawing on the theoretical framework of algorithmic imaginaries, this study investigates how Chinese parent vloggers of autistic children on Douyin imagine and enact their relationships with algorithms. Drawing primarily on in-depth interviews, supplemented by non-participant observation, we found that parent vloggers, driven by both material and spiritual motivations, perceive algorithms as playing three distinct roles: ‘judge,’ ‘butler,’ and ‘tool,’ representing strong, moderate, and weak tensions, respectively. The interplay between these algorithmic imaginaries and parent vloggers’ primary motivations shapes their exercise of agency on Douyin within their new media practices. This study thus calls for reconstructing localized and situated understandings of human–technology relations within disability-related media practices.

title: Trade Exposure and the Decline in Collective Bargaining: Evidence From Germany
abstract: ABSTRACT We analyze how rising trade exposure from China and Eastern Europe affected collective bargaining coverage in German plants from 1996 to 2008. Using cross‐industry variation in trade exposure and instrumenting with trade flows from other high‐income countries, we find that higher import exposure increased the likelihood that plants exited industry‐wide bargaining agreements, while export exposure had no average effect. Overall, rising trade exposure explains about 13% of the decline in industry‐wide bargaining coverage. The import effect is stronger for small and medium‐sized plants, while export opportunities help stabilize participation among large plants and those with works councils.
journal_name: Industrial Relations: A Journal of Economy and Society

title: Vertical consolidation and voter turnout: evidence from England
abstract: Structural reforms to local government have complex effects on electoral participation, especially when they involve the abolition of multiple tiers of government through the vertical consolidation of small authorities providing neighbourhood services and large authorities providing strategic services. Using a synthetic difference-in-differences approach, this paper analyses voter turnout across 13 election cycles (1973–2021) in five two-tier counties in England that were consolidated into single tier unitary authorities in 2009. The results suggest voter turnout increased in consolidated counties, a finding that could be explained by the smaller number of candidates per seat and weaker effective party competition in the initial period after consolidation. The implications of these findings are discussed.

title: A deep generative prediction framework for source–load forecasting in integrated energy systems
Post-contingency power network restoration for enhanced resilience: A drone-assisted approach
Climate- and nature-related transition risks in Brazil: capital stranding and financial vulnerability
abstract: Climate- and nature-related transition risks can generate economic impacts extending far beyond directly exposed sectors. We investigate these risks in Brazil by combining an input–output (IO) assessment of capital stranding with a firm-level analysis of financial vulnerability. Using both demand- and supply-driven input–output (IO) models, we assess sectors' exposure to capital stranding from transition shocks affecting fossil fuel extraction, agriculture, and forestry. We then classify firms and sectors according to their debt-servicing capacity to identify sectors where capital stranding overlaps with pre-existing financial fragility. Results highlight that both high- and low-pressuring sectors are exposed to capital stranding, with notable geographical spillovers – particularly to China. We also find that several of the most exposed sectors are already financially fragile, requiring debt rollover or being unable to meet their financial obligations. These findings suggest that climate- and nature-related transition risks can combine, exacerbating capital stranding and deepening existing vulnerabilities, while underscoring the importance of accounting for indirect exposures in transition risk assessments.

title: AI-generated advice as a reinforcement layer in climate-smart agriculture
abstract: Climate-smart agricultural (CSA) practices are central to food-system decarbonisation, yet adoption often falls short of farmers’ stated intentions, weakening the impact of incentives and extension under capacity constraints. We test whether spatially targeted, AI-generated advice can narrow this intention-action gap in a randomised field experiment with 1529 row crop farmers in Iowa, Illinois and Indiana during the cover crop decision window. Farmers assigned to receive four AI-generated emails were 4.45 %age points more likely to plant cover crops than controls (z = 2.81, p = 0.005), despite high baseline intentions in both groups. Effects operated on the extensive margin: there was no detectable change in the share of land planted among adopters. Survey responses indicate high engagement and a shift from untested optimism to more calibrated trust after exposure. Supervised AI advice can provide a low-cost, scalable complement to existing extension, improving follow-through and modestly expanding uptake without displacing human expertise.

title: Electricity prices during the energy crisis in Germany: The role of market power
Digital twins of wind turbine structures in the era of artificial intelligence: Evolution, applications, and future perspectives
abstract: The continuous upscaling of wind turbines and their deployment into increasingly challenging operational environments necessitates a fundamental evolution in structural asset management. In this context, the rise of Digital Twins in Engineering marks a pivotal moment, bringing a new era of technological innovation. This review traces the historical development of the Digital Twin concept and its diverse roles in engineering, critically synthesizes previously reported Digital Twin frameworks for wind turbine structures, and subsequently proposes a comprehensive, structure-centric Digital Twin framework tailored for offshore wind turbine support structures. It critically analyzes the enabling technologies that form the backbone of the system, including the integration of data acquisition from supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) and structural health monitoring (SHM) systems, advanced multi-physics simulation, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. A key component of this work is an in-depth categorization of Digital Twins applications, which encompass virtual sensing, dynamic performance monitoring, and advances in prognostics that facilitate a shift from corrective maintenance to preventive and condition-based maintenance. The present work also addresses global strategic initiatives and discusses primary technical and organizational bottlenecks, including persistent challenges in model credibility, computational efficiency, and data interoperability. The work concludes that the continued integration of these technologies provides the foundation for realizing fully lifecycle-aware Digital Twins, capable of transforming the management of this critical renewable energy infrastructure towards sustainability and resilience.

title: A decade of the belt and road initiative: Environmental implications, material footprints, and the next research frontier
Life cycle assessment of hydroponic container farm use in U.S. urban food system transitions
Matrix-Resolved Profiling of the Prenatal Chemical Exposome Reveals Selective Placental Retention and Fetal Transfer
abstract: Abstract Chemical exposure during human development, especially in utero, can disrupt many biological processes and increase disease vulnerability. Assessing the chemical landscape across the maternal–fetal interface is challenging. Here we address this challenge by conducting an exposome-based analysis across a suite of integrated maternal–fetal biological compartments: maternal urine, maternal serum, placental tissue, and umbilical cord serum. Using wide-scope liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) in 23 mother-infant dyads from the INSULIN cohort (Spain), we profiled 659 chemicals and transformation products, enabling a comprehensive characterization of prenatal chemical exposure and its compartment-specific distribution. We identified 76 unique compounds, including food additives, personal care products, pharmaceuticals, plasticizers, pesticides, flame retardants, industrial chemicals, and tobacco-related biomarkers. Matrix-resolved profiling revealed distinct compartmentalization patterns, with lipophilicity (logP) emerging as the primary physicochemical determinant of placental retention and transplacental transfer, while active transport mechanisms governed the fetal transfer of selected compounds despite properties inconsistent with passive diffusion. We report, for the first time, the transplacental passage of multiple emerging contaminants, including organophosphate esters, food-related compounds and personal care product ingredients. In contrast, several other contaminants─such as selected biomarkers of plastics, smoke, and personal care products─showed no evidence of transplacental transfer. These findings highlight the value of comprehensive, multi-matrix exposome profiling for assessing prenatal chemical exposures and provide a scalable framework for exposome-wide association studies in pregnancy cohorts and beyond.

title: Using Multimodal Large Language Models for Extracting Structured Life-Cycle Inventory Data from Scientific Literature
abstract: Abstract Life-cycle inventory (LCI) construction remains labor-intensive because relevant information is distributed across heterogeneous text, tables, and figures and is reported using inconsistent terminology, units, and system boundaries. Although large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for automated information extraction, LCI-specific workflows that reliably convert literature-reported information to structured and traceable inventory records remain limited. Here, we present LCIMiner, an automated LLM-based workflow integrating literature retrieval and screening, text-based selection of LCI-relevant figures and tables, multimodal information extraction, task-specific self-review, and structured LCI construction without model retraining. We evaluated LCIMiner in aquaculture, polymer production, and biofuel production, which differ substantially in their production processes, inventory structures, and reporting conventions. Across these domains, LCIMiner achieved higher end-to-end extraction performance than matched single-model baselines and converted heterogeneous literature evidence to machine-readable, source-traceable LCI records. We further applied a separate human-guided harmonization procedure to organize the extracted aquaculture records into a cross-study analytical data set while preserving the original source information. Together, the automated extraction workflow and subsequent human-guided harmonization provide a transparent and extensible approach for developing reusable foreground LCI data sets from heterogeneous scientific literature.

title: Beyond the Dominant Geological Metal(loid): Co-Occurring Metal(loid)s Are Linked to Microbial Assembly and Resistomes in Mercury-Enriched Soils
abstract: Abstract High geological background regions are naturally enriched with multiple, typically low bioavailability metal(loid)s. Superimposed mining, smelting, and agricultural inputs create complex yet poorly studied environments. Using metagenomics, we profiled bacterial community assembly and life history strategies in a mercury (Hg)-enriched geological area with elevated co-occurring metal(loid)s. Bacterial composition, structure, and community assembly, as well as the abundances of metal resistance genes (MRGs) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), were independent of Hg concentration. Instead, cadmium (Cd), ammonium nitrogen (NH4+-N), soil organic matter (SOM), and available potassium (AK) were significantly associated with ARG/MRG variation (p < 0.05). Moreover, elevated Cd intensified heterogeneous selection (HeS) while suppressing homogeneous selection (HoS) (p < 0.05). This shift also led communities enriched in “nutrient recycling” traits adopted a resource acquisition strategy together with competitor traits (MRGs and ARGs), and nitrogen metabolism. These traits likely reflect a strategy prioritizing resource use efficiency and nutrient competitiveness. Moreover, elevated Cd exacerbated the codissemination risks of resistance genes and pathogenicity (p < 0.001). Thus, Cd was more strongly associated than Hg with bacterial community and resistome variation in Hg-enriched geological soils, underscoring the need to consider co-occurring metal(loid)s when assessing ecological responses in high-background regions.

title: Unveiling the Underexplored Neurotoxicity of 2,6-Dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone: Insights from Network Toxicology and In Vivo Models
abstract: Abstract Halobenzoquinone disinfection byproducts (DBPs) are emerging drinking water contaminants with high toxic potency, among which 2,6-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone (2,6-DCBQ) is the most frequently detected. Despite the advances achieved in the toxicity of 2,6-DCBQ, its toxicological profile remains incompletely characterized. Herein, we integrated network toxicology with mouse and zebrafish models to explore the toxicity of 2,6-DCBQ. Network toxicology analysis highlighted neurotoxicity as a high-priority predicted end point and identified neuroinflammation and monoaminergic disruption as candidate molecular events. After 28 days of oral exposure, 2,6-DCBQ accumulated in a dose-dependent manner in the mouse brain and induced reactive gliosis and inflammatory responses, particularly in the prefrontal cortex and the hypothalamus. Most dopamine and serotonin receptors exhibited varying degrees of suppression, whereas HTR3A was consistently upregulated across all examined brain regions. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation provided preliminary evidence for the potential interaction between 2,6-DCBQ and HTR3A. In zebrafish larvae, environmentally relevant 2,6-DCBQ exposure also reduced dopaminergic neuron fluorescence and brain 5-HT levels and led to affective disorder-like behavior characterized by increased dark preference. These findings identify neuroinflammation and disrupted monoaminergic signaling as prominent features of 2,6-DCBQ-induced neurotoxicity and highlight the potential mental health risks of halobenzoquinone DBPs.

title: Potential Biodiversity Footprint Reductions from Intended Shifts to Plant-Based Meals
abstract: Abstract Adopting plant-based diets can mitigate biodiversity loss by reducing the demand for land required for feed and livestock. Yet, most assessments rely on hypothetical dietary scenarios that potentially overestimate biodiversity gains. We conducted a large-scale consumer survey across three countries (NLD, GBR, and USA) and estimated the biodiversity footprints of current and intended future diets using the loss of mean species abundance (MSA-loss) and the loss of global species richness (RSR-loss) as indicators. Over half of the respondents expressed no intention to reduce meat or dairy consumption. Among those intending to replace meat with plant-based alternatives, biodiversity footprints based on MSA-loss associated with the consumption of meat and plant-based alternatives in main meals would decrease by up to 34% on average. When considering all respondents, the average reduction in MSA-loss from meat and meat alternatives in the three countries would be 13%. We found similar results for current and intended future consumption of dairy and their plant-based alternatives. RSR-loss showed the same patterns as MSA-loss, although dairy alternatives would contribute a large share of the total biodiversity footprint based on RSR-loss in the USA. Our findings show that intended dietary shifts may not match hypothetical dietary scenarios and that achieving sustainable dietary shifts to reduce biodiversity loss remains a considerable challenge.

title: Building Footprint Has a Stronger Land Surface Temperature Signal than Building Height across Global Cities
abstract: Abstract Urban heat is a growing environmental challenge as cities expand and densify. The thermal meaning of added built volume depends on whether volume is produced through larger building footprint, greater building height, or both. Using 2020 hottest-month land surface temperature (LST) and global building data on a common 1 km grid for 1,480 cities, we quantified within-city spatial associations between LST anomalies and building-volume density. We defined the corresponding coefficient as the building volume response (BVR). We separated BVR into the footprint pathway response (BVR-F) and height pathway response (BVR-H). Across these cities, the median BVR was 4.6 × 10–3 °C per 1% difference in building-volume density, and BVR was estimated to be positive in 1,107 cities (74.8%). Median BVR-F and BVR-H were 5.1 × 10–3 °C and 1.3 × 10–3 °C. Under the prespecified near-equal band of ± 0.01 °C on the common 10% scale, 917 cities, or 62.0%, had a larger footprint response. The pathway contrast varied with vegetation structure, surface replacement, land cover, and climate context. These results provide a global basis for interpreting urban densification through land occupation and vertical stacking and for identifying surface contexts where footprint oriented growth is more closely associated with hotter urban land surfaces.

title: Reinforcement-Learning-Enabled Supervisory Control of a Full-Scale Anaerobic Digestion Facility Using a Calibrated Digital Twin
abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) is a cornerstone of energy recovery and decarbonization at wastewater resource recovery facilities (WRRFs), yet full-scale digesters are often operated conservatively due to delayed process feedback, nonlinear stability constraints, and limited observability. This study presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL)-enabled supervisory control framework for full-scale AD that integrates a calibrated mechanistic digital twin model (DTM) with offline policy learning and counterfactual uncertainty evaluation. Specifically, the DTM was calibrated to reproduce control-relevant digester behavior. Using 2.7 years of simulated operation, a batch-constrained Q (BCQ)-reinforcement learning policy was trained to maximize biogas production while penalizing instability associated with pH excursions and elevated volatile fatty acids (VFAs)/alkalinity (ALK) ratios. Counterfactual evaluation against historical, greedy, and heuristic controls used 1 year unseen DTM simulation and 1 year of full-scale operational data. The RL policy achieved comparable mean daily biogas production (+0.35%) in simulated testing. Under the 1 year operational data, it achieved plant-equivalent mean production of 9802 m3/day, corresponding to a modest potential cumulative improvement (+2.7%, 93 405 m3/year) subject to substantial uncertainty P(Δ > 0) = 0.524. These results indicate that offline-trained RL, combined with a mechanistic digital twin and counterfactual evaluation, provides a feasible and interpretable framework for developing and assessing supervisory AD control without live-plant experimentation while showing that the resulting benefit must be interpreted under explicit model-plant uncertainty.

title: One Quarter of Global Data Centers are Located in Water-Stressed Areas
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of digital services is increasing the demand for high-performance computing within data centers, intensifying the demand for local natural resources, particularly energy and water. This study assesses the current and future exposure of all 9347 currently identified data centers worldwide to water gap conditions, areas where water demand exceeds available supply, resulting in unsustainable water consumption and an increase in water stress. We find that 25% of data centers would already have experienced at least 1 month of water gap annually under 2001–2010 hydrologic conditions. While such conditions rarely prevent continued operation, they intensify stress with other water-dependent sectors. 33% of currently identified data centers would be in regions experiencing water gaps under future hydrological conditions. Data centers overlap with water demands from municipal (41%), irrigation (28%), manufacturing (18%), and power generation (8%) sectors. The United States hosts 39% of data centers, with 21% located in water-scarce regions, where overlap with municipal and agricultural demands is pronounced. The extent to which water-stress exposure translates into operational impacts for data centers themselves or into measurable consequences for other water users remains an open question to address. Ensuring data center long-term viability will require siting and governance choices that account for local hydrological limits.

Techno-economic optimisation of multi-sector coupled energy systems: A 1 GW electrolyser case study in Esbjerg, Denmark
abstract: This study evaluates the techno-economic performance of a multi-sector energy system coupling Power-to-X, district heating, and district cooling. A 1 GW electrolyser was coupled to the existing district heating system in Esbjerg, Denmark, through heat-recovery and cooling pathways that allocate excess heat between district heating and district cooling while maintaining the required thermal conditions. A techno-economic mixed-integer linear programming model was developed to optimise hourly operations, integrating merit-order dispatch and mass-flow dynamics. Three system configurations were assessed: a fully coupled Power-to-X, district heating, and district cooling system; a Power-to-X and district cooling system without district heating integration; and a reference district heating system. The results show that coupling Power-to-X, district heating, and district cooling creates cross-sector synergies between industrial hydrogen production and local energy system operations. The fully coupled system increased district heating performance factor by 7%, reducing annual heating costs by 15%. District cooling operating costs were reduced by 23%. The electrolyser’s excess heat generates 58 million DKK/yr in heat revenue, while district-heating pre-cooling avoids 21 million DKK/yr in cooling costs. This two-fold benefit improves Power-to-X operation and leads to 191 million DKK/yr in additional hydrogen sales.

title: Experimental and numerical Investigation of an integrated PVT–TEC–VMED system for off-grid freshwater production
abstract: Existing off-grid solar desalination systems are often constrained by inefficient thermal-energy utilization, inadequate waste-heat recovery, and unstable operation under fluctuating solar conditions, resulting in reduced freshwater productivity and overall system efficiency. To address these limitations, this study experimentally evaluated a thermally integrated hybrid freshwater production system. The system integrates a photovoltaic–thermal (PVT) collector, a thermoelectric module (TEM), a vertical multi-effect diffusion (VMED) desalination unit, and thermal and electrical energy-storage subsystems. The proposed configuration simultaneously harnessed solar energy for electricity generation, thermal-energy recovery, saline-water preheating, atmospheric moisture condensation, and desalination under fully off-grid operating conditions. System performance was experimentally investigated at feed salinity levels of 10,000, 20,000, and 30,000 ppm over a 12-day test period. The maximum freshwater productivity reached 23.05 kg/day at a feed salinity of 10,000 ppm, whereas the minimum productivity was 14.50 kg/day at 30,000 ppm. Year-long TRNSYS simulations predicted an average daily freshwater productivity of approximately 35.03 kg/day under continuous autonomous operation with thermal and electrical energy storage. The experimental results were compared with predictions from the TRNSYS model, yielding an R 2 of 0.805, an RMSE of 1.383 kg, and a maximum deviation of approximately 11%. Water-quality analysis confirmed effective salt removal, and the produced freshwater met the World Health Organization (WHO) drinking-water standards. Furthermore, the minimum freshwater production cost was estimated at 0.0025 USD/kg under favorable operating conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate that the synergistic integration of PVT cooling, TEM waste-heat recovery, and VMED desalination substantially improves freshwater productivity, thermal-energy utilization, and operational stability, offering an effective approach to sustainable and decentralized freshwater production.

title: A possible mediating role of SASP in the association between environmental air pollution and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
abstract: Cellular senescence is a state of cell cycle arrest with the loss of capacity for replication. Senescent cells produce molecules called the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which mediate the damaging effects of senescent cells, and also signal nearby cells to become senescent. Senescence has been linked to numerous diseases, including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Particulate matter less than 2.5 μm in aerodynamic diameter (PM 2.5 ) has also been associated with ASCVD, as well as cellular senescence. Our aim was to evaluate whether SASP mediated the effect of PM 2.5 exposure on incident ASCVD. Data were from 38,261 participants in the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) who resided within 400 km of Greater London, including air pollution exposure measured in 2010, plasma proteomic measurements collected at baseline, and incident ASCVD ascertained through electronic health records over a mean follow-up of 13.3 years. The SASP index was derived as the first principal component of 94 SASP-related proteins selected a priori. A one–standard deviation (SD) increase in the SASP index was significantly associated with a 12.9% higher risk of incident ASCVD (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 1.129; 95% CI 1.096 to 1.164). PM 2.5 exposure was positively associated with the SASP index (0.026 SD increase per interquartile range [IQR]; 95% CI 0.014 to 0.038) and with incident ASCVD (aHR = 1.059; 95% CI, 1.023 to 1.098 per IQR). The SASP index demonstrated a statistically significant mediation effect in the association between PM 2.5 exposure and incident ASCVD (indirect effect as log(aHR) = 0.0032 mediated through the SASP index, 95% CI 0.0017 to 0.0049), accounting for 5.52% of the total association. The potential mediating role of the SASP index offers insight into a potential mechanism of how senescence may be associated with cardiovascular disease. Further research is warranted to validate our findings and inform the development of targeted public health interventions.

Robust decision-making for minimizing building life-cycle GHG emissions and costs under uncertainties: Application to office buildings in China's cold regions
abstract: Uncertainties can substantially affect building life-cycle assessment (LCA) results. Existing optimization methods commonly adopt certainty assumptions and limited variables without sufficient robustness interpretation. This study develops a probabilistic decision-making framework for minimizing life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions (LCGHG) and life-cycle costs (LCC) under deterministic, mean, and 90th percentile (P90) risk metrics, which is applied to multistorey office building design in China's cold regions. The life-cycle performances of nine stock-derived form prototypes, combined with envelopes, HVAC, and rooftop photovoltaics, are explored under uncertain future climate, grid mix, discount rates, and component lifespans. Pareto-diagrams show that solutions obtained from different robustness criteria fall into two performance clusters mainly distinguished by HVAC energy sources. Yet deterministic and mean-based Pareto-fronts demonstrate materially higher upper-tail values of LCGHG and/or LCC. P90-based optimal ground-source heat pump solutions achieve LCGHG (90%) of 22.79–23.57 kg CO 2 -eq./(m 2 ·a) and LCC (90%) of 4558–5518 CNY/m 2 , whereas air-source heat pump solutions reduce costs by approximately 50% but increase emissions by about 30%. Within each cluster, building forms further differentiate performances, while envelopes and photovoltaics fine-tune outcomes. Design ranking consistency and performance distributional analyses indicate that solutions with lower P90 values generally correspond to lower medians and narrower variations. Moreover, P90-optimal solutions show similar operational emissions with trade-offs between equipment-related embodied emissions and costs. Sensitivity analysis identifies grid mix and HVAC lifespans as key drivers of LCGHG uncertainty, whereas discount rates and HVAC lifespans govern LCC variability. Although numerical findings are specific to the case, the proposed workflow and design guidance are transferable to other contexts.

title: Social protection as climate adaptation: Evidence from Pakistan’s Benazir Income Support Programme in mitigating food insecurity under rainfall and flood shocks
abstract: Climate-induced shocks pose a growing threat to food security in climate-vulnerable countries, particularly in South Asia. This study examines whether participation in Pakistan’s Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), one of the largest unconditional cash transfer initiatives in the Global South, is associated with greater household food-security resilience during rainfall and flood shocks. Using four rounds of household panel data (2011–2016) merged with tehsil-level meteorological and flood-exposure data. We estimate GLS panel models with interaction terms. Results show that rainfall and flood shocks are associated with lower household calorie intake and dietary diversity, thereby worsening food insecurity among vulnerable populations. However, during shock periods, BISP beneficiaries experience significantly better food-security outcomes than non-recipients. The interaction estimates further show that the programme’s buffering association varies across shock types. The association is strongest and most robust for calorie intake and calorie-based food-security status under rainfall shocks. Evidence is weaker for dietary diversity and less consistent under floods, particularly at higher flood severity. Because programme participation is not randomly assigned, the estimates are interpreted as moderating associations rather than definitive causal effects. These findings highlight the dual role of social protection programmes as both poverty alleviation tools and climate adaptation mechanisms. We discuss policy implications for integrating cash transfers into broader climate resilience strategies, including disaster risk reduction, climate-resilient infrastructure, and localized adaptation planning in emerging Asian regions.

title: Examining challenges and uncertainties associated with using water table management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from grassland peat soils
abstract: Countries with significant areas of grassland on organic soils must accurately estimate the extents of these lands to estimate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from them. These areas are often targeted for management change to reduce emissions reported under the Land Use, Land Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) sector in national GHG emission inventories. The present study aims to assess the extent of grassland on organic soils across the European Union (EU) and their associated GHG emissions and utilises a systematic review process to quantify the potential effectiveness of efforts to raise the water table level on such lands. Additionally, using Ireland as a case study, different scenarios that incorporate varied levels of water table management, together with the reported extent and classification of nutrient and drainage status of these lands, enable a broad range of GHG emissions to be estimated. If Ireland were to meet its target of reducing the management intensity of 80,000 ha of drained organic soil under grassland, emissions from these lands will potentially reduce by 590.44 kt CO 2 -eq yr −1 . It may be difficult to fully rewet these lands, so other scenarios were also considered to demonstrate the potential emission reductions associated with raising the water table level from the currently assumed deeply drained status to shallow drained or a combination of both shallow drained and rewetted status. These scenarios provide a framework to explore different pathways to meet emission reduction targets for countries with significant extents of grassland on organic soils.

title: Fossil fuel dependence and environmental sustainability: Insights from SDGs 7 and 13 in gulf economies
abstract: This study presents the first empirical unification of the Environmental Phillips Curve (EPC) and Tragedy of the Commons (TOC) frameworks in fossil-fuel-dependent Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies. Employing a Cross-Sectional Autoregressive Distributed Lag approach on data from 2000 to 2023, the analysis accounts for cross-sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity across GCC states. The results show that a 1% increase in non-renewable energy capacity raises CO 2 emissions by 8.09%, quantitatively confirming the carbon lock-in mechanism central to the TOC framework. Conversely, foreign direct investment (FDI) significantly improves ecological balance ( β = 0.0248), supporting the pollution halo hypothesis, whereas unemployment reduces CO 2 emissions but presents complex trade-offs for broader ecological health. Financial development and economic globalisation are shown to degrade environmental quality. These findings provide robust empirical validation for both theoretical frameworks: the EPC is confirmed through nuanced unemployment–environment dynamics in the GCC's segmented labour market, and the TOC is operationalised via carbon lock-in effects. The study advances theoretical integration and offers actionable policy insights to reconcile economic development with ecological sustainability in resource-dependent regions, thereby advancing Sustainable Development Goals 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and 13 (Climate Action) through green investment and transition strategies.

title: GLP-1 drugs fail to help some people lose weight — scientists are on a quest for answers
